title: Simulation in Gazebo: worlds, sensors, a camera in ROS 2 and scenario tests
summary: SITL без внешнего симулятора считает физику простой встроенной моделью и не знает, что такое дерево, стена или изображение с камеры. Для зрения, обхода препятствий, точной посадки и подвесов нужен мир: Gazebo даёт физику, освещение, камеры, лидары и дальномеры, а автопилот работает с ним как с насто
headings: Какой Gazebo Как автопилот говорит с миром Мир на SDF Датчики и мост в ROS 2 Скорость и ресурсы HITL и SITL Сценарные тесты Шаг 1. Iris в Gazebo Шаг 2. Свой мир со столбом Шаг 3. Камера в ROS 2 Шаг 4. Сценарный тест
text: summary SITL без внешнего симулятора считает физику простой встроенной моделью и не знает, что такое дерево, стена или изображение с камеры. Для зрения, обхода препятствий, точной посадки и подвесов нужен мир: Gazebo даёт физику, освещение, камеры, лидары и дальномеры, а автопилот работает с ним как с настоящим аппаратом. Модуль разбирает связку ArduPilot SITL и PX4 SITL с Gazebo новым, gz , устройство мира на SDF, добавление препятствия и камеры, мост изображений в ROS 2, сценарные тесты без графики для CI и что такое HITL и чем он отличается от SITL. theory Какой Gazebo - Gazebo gz — новая линейка бывший Ignition . Для ROS 2 Jazzy парная LTS-версия — Gazebo Harmonic ; её же рекомендует плагин ArduPilot. - Gazebo Classic gazebo11 закончил поддержку в январе 2025 — старые инструкции с gazebo --verbose и .world для Classic не переносить. - Пара «ROS 2 — Gazebo» фиксирована: смешивать версии мимо рекомендованных пар — источник трудноуловимых проблем со сборкой мостов. Как автопилот говорит с миром - ArduPilot : плагин ardupilot_gazebo система ArduPilotPlugin в модели . Gazebo считает физику и датчики, плагин отправляет состояние в SITL и получает от него команды моторам/сервам; обмен — JSON по UDP, в режиме lockstep симуляция ждёт автопилот, время согласовано . Запуск: в одном терминале gz sim -v4 -r iris_runway.sdf , в другом sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter -f gazebo-iris --model JSON --map --console . Имя фрейма должно содержать gazebo- , модель — JSON . - PX4 : Gazebo встроен в сборку SITL: make px4_sitl gz_x500 ; варианты моделей с датчиками например gz_x500_depth , gz_x500_mono_cam и самолёты/VTOL; мир выбирается переменной PX4_GZ_WORLD . - Переменные окружения: GZ_SIM_SYSTEM_PLUGIN_PATH — где искать плагины сборка ardupilot_gazebo , GZ_SIM_RESOURCE_PATH — модели и миры. Мир на SDF Мир — XML-файл SDF: физика шаг, например 1 мс , освещение, земля, модели. Модель — звенья link с геометрией столкновений collision и видимой visual , массой и инерцией, суставы joint , датчики sensor и системы-плагины. Препятствие — статическая модель: xml <model name="pole" <static true</static <pose 10 0 5 0 0 0</pose <link name="link" <collision name="collision" <geometry <cylinder <radius 0.3</radius <length 10</length </cylinder </geometry </collision <visual name="visual" <geometry <cylinder <radius 0.3</radius <length 10</length </cylinder </geometry </visual </link </model Столб 10 м высотой, в 10 м к востоку от начала координат мира ENU: x — восток, y — север, z — вверх . Датчики и мост в ROS 2 - Камеры, камеры глубины, лидары gpu_lidar , IMU — элементы sensor в модели; публикуют в шину Gazebo gz-transport , список — gz topic -l . - ros_gz_bridge переносит топики между Gazebo и ROS 2: ros2 run ros_gz_bridge parameter_bridge /camera@sensor_msgs/msg/Image@gz.msgs.Image — имя топика, тип ROS 2, тип Gazebo; @ — в обе стороны, — из Gazebo в ROS, — из ROS в Gazebo. - Отдельный плагин GstCameraPlugin из ardupilot_gazebo отдаёт видео с камеры по GStreamer H.264, UDP 5600 — как настоящая камера на companion; поток включается сообщением в топик .../enable_streaming . Пример мира с подвесом и камерой — gimbal.sdf ; подвес Iris в iris_runway.sdf SITL с gazebo-iris-gimbal.parm управляется каналами RC6–RC8. - Реализм: идеальная камера без шума и размытия обманывает — алгоритмы зрения стоит проверять с шумом, сменой освещения и размытием движения параметры шума в описании датчика . Скорость и ресурсы - Real-time factor RTF — отношение скорости симуляции к реальному времени; с камерами и лидарами на слабой машине падает ниже 1. Lockstep сохраняет корректность, но тест длится дольше. - Рендеринг нужен только датчикам изображения; для тестов логики без камер — сервер без графики gz sim -s -r мир.sdf , для камер на машине без экрана — режим --headless-rendering . HITL и SITL - SITL — прошивка собрана под компьютер, всё виртуальное. - HITL hardware in the loop — настоящий полётник со своей прошивкой, датчики подменяются данными симулятора по USB/MAVLink, моторы не крутятся. Проверяет реальное железо: тайминги, загрузку процессора, драйверы, что SITL скрывает. Поддержка и способ настройки отличаются у PX4 и ArduPilot и между версиями — по документации своей версии. Сценарные тесты Сценарий — воспроизводимый полёт с проверкой результата: «взлёт на 10 м, облёт столба, посадка; не ближе 2 м к столбу, высота в допуске». Запуск без графики, проверка через MAVLink и лог, результат — pass/fail для CI модуль «Конфигурации в CI» . Один сценарий на каждую функцию безопасности failsafe, геозона, RTL ловит регрессии при обновлении прошивки и параметров раньше поля. {{diagram:gazebo-sitl Gazebo считает физику и датчики, плагин обменивается с SITL по JSON в lockstep; изображения идут в ROS 2 через ros_gz_bridge, наземка и тесты подключаются к SITL по MAVLink.}} practice Шаг 1. Iris в Gazebo Установить Gazebo Harmonic и собрать ardupilot_gazebo по README зависимости, cmake , make , выставить GZ_SIM_SYSTEM_PLUGIN_PATH и GZ_SIM_RESOURCE_PATH . Запустить iris_runway.sdf и SITL с -f gazebo-iris --model JSON . Взлёт в GUIDED на 10 м из MAVProxy. Записать RTF при висении. Шаг 2. Свой мир со столбом Скопировать iris_runway.sdf в свой мир, добавить столб из теории. Миссия: взлёт, точка в 20 м к востоку на высоте 5 м, возврат. Что происходит с аппаратом без обхода препятствий? Перенести точку так, чтобы маршрут проходил в 3 м от столба. Шаг 3. Камера в ROS 2 Запустить мир с камерой gimbal.sdf или модель с камерой , найти топик изображения gz topic -l , поднять мост в ROS 2 и проверить ros2 topic hz и rqt_image_view или ros2 run image_tools showimage . Записать частоту кадров и разрешение. Шаг 4. Сценарный тест pytest-сценарий против SITL Gazebo без графики: gz sim -s -r мир.sdf : python import time from pymavlink import mavutil def test_takeoff_hold_land : m = mavutil.mavlink_connection "udpin:0.0.0.0:14550" m.wait_heartbeat timeout=30 m.set_mode "GUIDED" deadline = time.time + 60 while not m.motors_armed : pre-arm checks pass once EKF and GPS a

title: Missions and planning
summary: A mission in ArduPilot is a list of commands the flight controller executes on its own in AUTO mode: take off, fly through waypoints, take a picture, come back. This module explains what a mission is made of, how navigation commands differ from DO and CONDITION commands, how altitude is calculated,
headings: Three types of commands Altitude Home Starting and resuming Failsafe during a mission Mission file Commands worth knowing by heart Altitudes: three frames and one mistake Worked example: surveying a 300×200 m area Step 1. A mission in SITL via the GCS Step 2. The same mission from code Step 3. Scenarios on top of a route
text: summary A mission in ArduPilot is a list of commands the flight controller executes on its own in AUTO mode: take off, fly through waypoints, take a picture, come back. This module explains what a mission is made of, how navigation commands differ from DO and CONDITION commands, how altitude is calculated, where home is, and what happens when the link is lost mid-route. Practice is in SITL, following the “route separately, scenario separately” pattern. theory Three types of commands - NAV — where to fly. NAV_TAKEOFF 22 , NAV_WAYPOINT 16 , NAV_LOITER_TIME 19 , NAV_RETURN_TO_LAUNCH 20 , NAV_LAND 21 . The mission goes from one NAV command to the next. - DO — what to do along the way without changing the route: DO_CHANGE_SPEED 178 , DO_SET_SERVO 183 , DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST 206 , DO_JUMP 177 for loops. - CONDITION — wait for a condition before the next DO command: CONDITION_DELAY 112 , CONDITION_DISTANCE . The numbers in parentheses are MAV_CMD codes: that's how the commands look in a mission file and in MAVLink. Altitude Every waypoint has a reference frame. For missions you almost always use altitude relative to home MAV_FRAME_GLOBAL_RELATIVE_ALT , code 3 : “100 m” means 100 m above the arming point. Absolute altitude above sea level MAV_FRAME_GLOBAL , 0 is rarely needed and easily leads to an error of hundreds of meters. Altitude above terrain requires terrain data. Home For Copter, the home point is where the aircraft armed. RTL returns there, not to where the pilot is standing. If you took off from the roof of a car and then drove somewhere else — home stayed at the old spot. In the GCS you can reset home before takeoff. Starting and resuming A Copter mission usually starts with NAV_TAKEOFF . Switching to AUTO on the ground with the aircraft armed starts the takeoff once the pilot raises the throttle or immediately, if bit 1 “Allow Takeoff Without Raising Throttle” is set in AUTO_OPTIONS ; in SITL — rc 3 1500 . By default, when you re-enter AUTO the mission continues from the current command; the MIS_RESTART parameter makes it start from the first one. Failsafe during a mission Loss of the radio link during AUTO behaves per FS_THR_ENABLE RTL, Land, SmartRTL… , and continuing the mission is enabled by bit 0 of FS_OPTIONS . For autonomous beyond-visual-line-of-sight flights this decision is made before takeoff, not after the fact. GCS loss is a separate parameter, FS_GCS_ENABLE . The battery failsafe BATT_FS_LOW_ACT , BATT_FS_CRT_ACT overrides the mission. Mission file GCSs save the mission to a text file in the QGC WPL 110 format: one line per command — index, current flag, frame, command code, four parameters, latitude, longitude, altitude, autocontinue flag. Such a file is convenient to keep in git next to the parameters. Commands worth knowing by heart NAV: NAV_WAYPOINT p1 — delay at the waypoint, s , NAV_TAKEOFF alt , NAV_LAND , NAV_RETURN_TO_LAUNCH , NAV_LOITER_TIME/TURNS/UNLIM , NAV_SPLINE_WAYPOINT spline , NAV_DELAY ; DO: DO_SET_SERVO , DO_SET_RELAY , DO_DIGICAM_CONTROL , DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST a shot every N m — the basis of photogrammetry , DO_CHANGE_SPEED , DO_SET_ROI point the gimbal/nose , DO_JUMP a loop, with a counter , DO_LAND_START the entry point of the landing sequence for a failsafe , DO_SET_HOME ; CONDITION: CONDITION_DELAY , CONDITION_DISTANCE , CONDITION_YAW . Execution parameters: WP_SPD m/s horizontal , WP_SPD_UP/DN , WP_RADIUS_M acceptance radius , WP_ACC before 4.7 — WPNAV_SPEED in cm/s, WPNAV_SPEED_UP/DN , WPNAV_RADIUS , WPNAV_ACCEL , WP_YAW_BEHAVIOR nose along the course or not , MIS_RESTART 0 — resume from the last command when entering Auto, 1 — from the start , MIS_OPTIONS bit 0 — clear the mission on reboot; bit 1 — use distance to landing in the battery failsafe Plane only ; bit 2 — continue after landing , RTL_ for the end of the mission. Altitudes: three frames and one mistake Relative above home, MAV_FRAME_GLOBAL_RELATIVE_ALT , the default , absolute above sea level — wrong if you take off somewhere else , terrain above ground from SRTM data via the GCS or from a rangefinder, TERRAIN_ENABLE , the “Terrain” frame on waypoints and WP_RFND_USE / RTL_ALT_TYPE . The classic crash: a mission with absolute altitudes, made for a different site 300 m higher — the aircraft tries to dive into the ground or climb into the sky. The rule: relative altitudes, and check the altitude-above-terrain profile in the GCS. Worked example: surveying a 300×200 m area Mission Planner → Survey Grid : camera sensor, focal length , altitude 80 m, overlap 75/65% → the planner calculates the spacing between survey lines and DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST itself; speed 8 m/s based on camera exposure: motion blur ≤ 1 px → v·t_exp ≤ GSD ; NAV_TAKEOFF 80, survey lines, DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST 0 at the end, NAV_RETURN_TO_LAUNCH . Checks: the altitude profile, mission time vs. battery capacity BATT_LOW_MAH with margin for RTL + capacity margin for the return , a geofence around the area. A run in SITL with the same mission file is mandatory. {{diagram:mission-alt-frames Choosing the altitude frame in a mission: Relative for flat ground, Terrain for varying terrain, Absolute when altitude above sea level is given.}} practice Step 1. A mission in SITL via the GCS 1. Start SITL: sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter --console --map . 2. In Mission Planner Plan or QGC Plan , set TAKEOFF 20 m, three waypoints, RTL. 3. Write the mission to the aircraft, save the .waypoints file. 4. Arm, AUTO mode, watch. Then try switching to LOITER mid-route and back to AUTO. Step 2. The same mission from code The route is data, the scenario is commands. An example of uploading a route via pymavlink: python from pymavlink import mavutil ROUTE = lat, lon, alt_m — data only, no commands here -35.3630, 149.1652, 30 , -35.3625, 149.1660, 30 , -35.3632, 149.1668, 30 , m = mavutil.mavlink_connection "tcp:127.0.0.1:5762" m.wait_heartbeat FRAME = mavutil.mavlink.MAV_FRAME_GLOBAL_RELATIVE_ALT_INT 6 def item seq, cmd, lat=0, lon=0, alt=0, p1

title: Guidance and trajectories: pure pursuit, L1, S-curves, minimum snap
summary: Регуляторы курса держат угол, скорость и позицию. Но кто решает, *какую* позицию держать в каждый момент, чтобы аппарат прошёл по линии миссии, плавно повернул и не дёрнулся? Это наведение и генерация траекторий. Модуль разбирает слои от миссии до регулятора, закон pure pursuit и его родственника L1
headings: Слои: от точек к моторам Pure pursuit L1 в ArduPlane и NPFG в PX4 Профили скорости: трапеция и S-кривая Minimum snap для квадрокоптера Feedforward: не только позиция Шаг 1. Pure pursuit в симуляции Шаг 2. L1 своего самолёта Шаг 3. Трапеция и S-кривая Шаг 4. SITL: рывок и скругление
text: summary Регуляторы курса держат угол, скорость и позицию. Но кто решает, какую позицию держать в каждый момент, чтобы аппарат прошёл по линии миссии, плавно повернул и не дёрнулся? Это наведение и генерация траекторий. Модуль разбирает слои от миссии до регулятора, закон pure pursuit и его родственника L1 в ArduPlane с формулой дальности упреждения через NAVL1_PERIOD , профили скорости — трапецию и S-кривую с ограничением рывка, которой ArduCopter ведёт по точкам, — и minimum snap для квадрокоптера с объяснением, почему именно «snap». Код симуляции воспроизводит графики модуля; лабораторная — подобрать упреждение по перелёту и времени выхода на линию. theory Слои: от точек к моторам 1. Миссия — список точек и действий модуль «Миссии» . 2. Путь — геометрия между точками: отрезки, дуги поворота, сплайны NAV_SPLINE_WAYPOINT . 3. Траектория — путь с временем: где аппарат должен быть в момент t, с какой скоростью и ускорением, в пределах ограничений скорости, ускорения и рывка. 4. Наведение / слежение — превращает отклонение от пути или траектории в команду ускорение, крен, скорость для регулятора позиции. Следование пути path following не заботится о времени — главное быть на линии. Слежение за траекторией trajectory tracking требует быть в точке вовремя — для строя, синхронной съёмки, совместных манёвров. Pure pursuit Аппарат «гонится» за точкой на пути, лежащей на расстоянии L впереди дальность упреждения . Если α — угол между вектором скорости и направлением на эту точку, то кривизна, выводящая на неё по дуге, κ = 2·sin α / L, а боковое ускорение a = V²·κ = 2·V²·sin α / L. - Малое L — резкий выход на линию, перелёт и чувствительность к шуму позиции. - Большое L — плавно, но медленно, и углы маршрута «срезаются». - При 20 м сбоку и 10 м/с симуляция ниже : L = 8 м — перелёт ~3 м; L = 20 м — перелёт ~1 м, в коридоре ±1 м через 35 м пути; L = 45 м — в коридоре только через ~90 м. {{diagram:chart-pure-pursuit Pure pursuit с 20 м сбоку при 10 м/с: малое упреждение даёт перелёт, большое — долгий выход на линию.}} L1 в ArduPlane и NPFG в PX4 L1 — тот же закон бокового ускорения в ArduPilot с коэффициентом 4ζ² вместо 2: a = 4ζ²·V²·sin η / L1, при ζ = 0.707 — ровно pure pursuit , но дальность упреждения растёт со скоростью, чтобы динамика выхода на линию не зависела от скорости: L1 = 1/π ·ζ·T·V, где T = NAVL1_PERIOD , ζ = NAVL1_DAMPING , V — путевая скорость. - Пример: V = 18 м/с, T = 17 с, ζ = 0.75 → L1 ≈ 0.318·0.75·17·18 ≈ 73 м. - Уменьшение NAVL1_PERIOD укорачивает L1 — резче повороты, риск вилять настройка — в модуле «Тюнинг ArduPlane» . - Боковое ускорение превращается в крен: tan φ = a / g, с ограничением ROLL_LIMIT_DEG . В PX4 для самолётов наведение ведёт NPFG nonlinear path following guidance : тот же принцип упреждения плюс явная обработка ветра, сравнимого со скоростью самолёта, — когда удержать линию нельзя, NPFG выбирает выполнимое направление, а не «сдувается» вбок. Параметры периода и демпфирования NPFG_PERIOD , NPFG_DAMPING — по смыслу как у L1. Профили скорости: трапеция и S-кривая - Трапеция : разгон с постоянным ускорением, крейсер, торможение. Ускорение меняется скачком — рывок производная ускорения бесконечен. Для коптера скачок ускорения = скачок наклона: дёрганье, раскачка груза и камеры, перерегулирование. - S-кривая jerk-limited : ускорение нарастает с ограниченным рывком. Перемещение на 50 м при v ≤ 10 м/с, a ≤ 5 м/с², рывок ≤ 10 м/с³: трапеция — 7.0 с, S-кривая — 7.5 с +0.5 с за время нарастания ускорения , но без скачков. - ArduCopter с 4.1 строит путь по точкам S-кривыми: скорость, ускорение и рывок задаются параметрами навигации WPNAV_SPEED , см/с; WPNAV_ACCEL , см/с²; WPNAV_JERK , м/с³; в Copter 4.7 — WP_SPD , м/с; WP_ACC , м/с²; WP_JERK , м/с³ , углы маршрута скругляются с радиусом WPNAV_RADIUS 4.7 — WP_RADIUS_M . {{diagram:chart-scurve Ускорение при перемещении на 50 м: трапеция переключает ускорение скачком, S-кривая — с ограниченным рывком, ценой 0.5 с.}} Minimum snap для квадрокоптера Квадрокоптер — дифференциально плоская система: зная траекторию позиции и курса, можно вычислить всё остальное. Тяга определяется ускорением, угловая скорость корпуса — рывком третьей производной позиции , а моменты моторов — snap четвёртой производной . Поэтому траектория с минимальным интегралом квадрата snap даёт самые гладкие команды моторам. На практике: между точками — полиномы 7-го порядка по каждой оси, непрерывные до snap в стыках, коэффициенты — из задачи квадратичной оптимизации Mellinger, Kumar, 2011 . Такие траектории строят на companion и отправляют автопилоту как цели позиции вместе со скоростью и ускорением feedforward , иначе регулятор позиции отстаёт. Feedforward: не только позиция Если companion шлёт только позицию, регулятор узнаёт, что надо разгоняться, когда ошибка уже есть, — аппарат отстаёт на поворотах. SET_POSITION_TARGET_LOCAL_NED позволяет передать позицию, скорость и ускорение одновременно маска type_mask : регулятор позиции догоняет только остаток ошибки. practice Шаг 1. Pure pursuit в симуляции Скрипт воспроизводит график модуля и считает перелёт и расстояние до входа в коридор ±1 м: python import math def pursuit L, y0=20.0, V=10.0, a_max=8.0, T=15.0, dt=0.02 : """Kinematic vehicle, path = the x axis. Returns overshoot m and distance to settle within 1 m.""" x, y, psi = 0.0, y0, 0.0 overshoot, settle_x = 0.0, None for _ in range int T / dt : dx = math.sqrt L L - y y if abs y < L else 0.0 lookahead point on the path alpha = math.atan2 -y, max dx, 0.5 - psi alpha = math.atan2 math.sin alpha , math.cos alpha a = max -a_max, min a_max, 2 V V math.sin alpha / L a_lat = 2V² sin α / L psi += a / V dt x += V math.cos psi dt y += V math.sin psi dt overshoot = max overshoot, -y if abs y 1.0: settle_x = None elif settle_x is None: settle_x = x return overshoot, settle_x for L in 8, 20, 45 : o, s = pursuit L print f"L = {L:2d} м: перелёт {o:.1f} м, в коридоре ±1 м с {s:.0f} м" L = 8 м: перелёт 3.0 м, в коридоре ±1 м с 35 м L = 20 м: перелёт 1.0 м, в коридоре ±1 м

title: ArduPilot logs: flight analysis
summary: ArduPilot writes a binary DataFlash log (`.bin`) to the SD card with hundreds of message types: attitude, altitude, motors, battery, EKF, errors. It's the black box that answers “why” after any weird flight. This module gives you an analysis order — from vibration to errors — with concrete message a
headings: Two kinds of logs Messages to start with Analysis order Tools Worked example: analyzing “a 3 m altitude drop in Loiter” Python for your own metrics (pymavlink) What to put in LOG_BITMASK Script: vibration and clipping from a log Lab Real log How to set up a motor failure in SITL What you should get and what to write down
text: summary ArduPilot writes a binary DataFlash log .bin to the SD card with hundreds of message types: attitude, altitude, motors, battery, EKF, errors. It's the black box that answers “why” after any weird flight. This module gives you an analysis order — from vibration to errors — with concrete message and field names, thresholds from the documentation, and a Python script for your own plots. theory Two kinds of logs - DataFlash .bin — onboard, high rate, everything. Your main tool. - Telemetry log .tlog — what the GCS saw over the radio link. Lower rate and with gaps, but it exists even if the SD card burned up along with the aircraft. The LOG_BITMASK parameter sets what gets logged; LOG_DISARMED enables logging before arming useful for analyzing pre-arm problems . Messages to start with - VIBE — vibration: VibeX , VibeY , VibeZ m/s² and Clip — the accelerometer saturation counter. Below 30 is normal; above 60 almost certainly means altitude and position problems. Clipping should be zero. - ATT — DesRoll vs. Roll , DesPitch vs. Pitch : how well the aircraft keeps up with the desired attitude. A sharp divergence means a mechanical problem or a lack of thrust. - CTUN — altitude control: ThO throttle output , ThH hover throttle estimate , DAlt / Alt desired and actual altitude , BAlt baro . - BAT — Volt , Curr , CurrTot , Res internal resistance estimate . Voltage sag under load and real consumption. - RCIN — radio channels C1…C14 : what the pilot was doing. - MODE — mode changes and the reason Rsn . - ERR — errors: Subsys and ECode . For example, subsystem 2 radio with code 2 — no receiver frames for two seconds; 11 — GPS glitch; 16 — bad EKF variance; 17 — EKF failsafe; 29 — vibration compensation. - MSG — text messages, including pre-arm ones. - GPS — NSats , HDop : HDOP below 1.5 is good, above 2.0 is suspicious; fewer than 12 satellites is bad. - XKF1…XKF4 — EKF3 internals per core: estimates and variances XKF4 : SV , SP , SH , SM — velocity, position, height, compass . - POWR — board VCC : fluctuations above 0.1–0.15 V hint at power problems. Analysis order 1. Does the log cut off? A log that ends in the air means power loss or a reboot. 2. Vibration VIBE . Everything else is meaningless while it's high. 3. Errors ERR , MSG : what triggered and when. 4. Modes MODE : who changed the mode — the pilot or a failsafe. 5. Control ATT , CTUN : did the aircraft keep up with commands. 6. Power BAT , POWR : sags and whether they coincide with events. 7. Navigation GPS , XKF4 : position quality and variances at the moment of the problem. Tools Mission Planner Review a Log , MAVExplorer from the MAVProxy package plots by field name, e.g. graph ATT.Roll ATT.DesRoll , UAV Log Viewer in the browser. For automation — pymavlink.DFReader : reads .bin directly in Python. Worked example: analyzing “a 3 m altitude drop in Loiter” 1. VIBE.VibeZ 12 m/s², Clip 0 → not vibration. 2. ERR / MSG : none. 3. CTUN : DAlt constant at 20 m, Alt drops to 17 m, BAlt at the same time → a real drop, not an estimation issue. 4. CTUN.ThO at that moment — 0.78 before — 0.42 , BAT.Volt 21.1 → 18.9 V, BAT.Curr 60 → 95 A: throttle hit the ceiling on a sagging battery. 5. RCIN.C3 — the pilot didn't touch the throttle; MODE has no changes. Conclusion: lack of thrust due to voltage sag on an old battery BAT.Res 0.09 Ω — high : replace the battery, use MOT_BAT_VOLT_MIN/MAX for compensation, raise the BATT_LOW_VOLT threshold. The method matters more than the conclusion: every step is a specific field. Python for your own metrics pymavlink python from pymavlink import mavutil import pandas as pd def df_of log, msg : m = mavutil.mavlink_connection log ; rows = while x := m.recv_match type=msg, blocking=False is not None: rows.append x.to_dict return pd.DataFrame rows att = df_of "flight.bin", "ATT" err = att.DesRoll - att.Roll .abs print "roll tracking RMS deg:", err.pow 2 .mean 0.5, "p99:", err.quantile 0.99 vibe = df_of "flight.bin", "VIBE" ; print "VibeZ p95:", vibe.VibeZ.quantile 0.95 , "clips:", vibe.Clip.max mavlogdump.py --types ATT,VIBE --format csv flight.bin — a quick CSV export with no code; MAVExplorer : graph ATT.Roll ATT.DesRoll , fft for batch-sampling spectra ISBH/ISBD , map for the trajectory. Step-response metrics and spectra are covered in the “Python for Data” module. What to put in LOG_BITMASK The default is enough for flight analysis; for tuning, add PID messages PIDR/PIDP/PIDY with P/I/D/FF per axis and IMU_RAW /batch sampling INS_LOG_BAT_MASK while you set up filters — the log grows several times over, so turn them off afterward. LOG_FILE_DSRMROT — a new file on every disarm; LOG_DISARMED = 1 — for ground measurements noise, GPS , then turn it off, otherwise the SD card fills up. {{diagram:log-triage Where to start analyzing a log: the symptom determines the first message — VIBE, BAT/POWR, XKF4/GPS, RATE/ATT or MODE/ERR/EV.}} practice Script: vibration and clipping from a log python import sys from pymavlink import DFReader log = DFReader.DFReader_binary sys.argv 1 vibe = {"VibeX": , "VibeY": , "VibeZ": } clip_max = 0 errors = while True: m = log.recv_msg if m is None: break t = m.get_type if t == "VIBE" and m.IMU == 0: for k in vibe: vibe k .append getattr m, k clip_max = max clip_max, m.Clip elif t == "ERR": errors.append m.TimeUS / 1e6, m.Subsys, m.ECode for k, v in vibe.items : v = sorted v print f"{k}: median {v len v //2 :.1f} p95 {v int len v 0.95 :.1f} m/s/s" print "accel clipping events:", clip_max for t, sub, code in errors: print f"ERR at {t:7.1f}s subsys={sub} ecode={code}" Run it: python vibe_report.py 00000012.BIN . A median above 30 or nonzero clipping — fix the mechanics first, then everything else. Lab 1. Fly a mission in SITL with a motor failure triggered by a switch. 2. text: summary ArduPilot can run Lua scripts right on the flight controller: add modes, read sensors, react to switches. In a training project the main use is fault injection: deliberately breaking a motor or sensor in SITL and watching how the drone and you cope. This module explains how scripting works, how to bind a script to a radio switch, and how to build a set of “chaos scripts,” each on its own switch. theory How scripting works - Enabled with the SCR_ENABLE = 1 parameter and a reboot. - Scripts .lua live in APM/scripts on the SD card; in SITL — in the scripts folder in the directory the simulator was launched from. - Each script runs in its own “sandbox” at low priority: flight code comes first, and nobody promises the script an exact schedule. - Script memory is set by SCR_HEAP_SIZE . Too little — scripts crash and a pre-arm error about insufficient memory appears. Too much — the EKF may fail to initialize. - If one script crashes with an error, only that script stops. If the shared script memory runs out or there's a panic , all scripts stop until a reboot. - Scripting requires at least 2 MB of flash and doesn't work on F4 controllers. The update pattern A script is an update function that does its work and returns itself and a delay in milliseconds until the next call. No infinite loops: the scheduler calls the function again on its own. Binding to a switch The RCx_OPTION parameter assigns a function to a radio channel. Values 300–307 are Scripting1…Scripting8: reserved for scripts. A script finds its channel via rc:find_channel_for_option 300 and reads the switch position via get_aux_switch_pos 0 — low, 1 — middle, 2 — high . Applets and examples The ArduPilot repository has ready-made scripts: libraries/AP_Scripting/applets ready to use, each with an .md description and libraries/AP_Scripting/examples learning examples . Start with the motor_failure_test.lua applet: it stops the motors set by the MOT_STOP_BITMASK bitmask when the Scripting1 switch is high. An octocopter should keep flying with one failed motor. What the API can do per docs/docs.lua in AP_Scripting Reading state: ahrs:get_position , ahrs:get_velocity_NED , ahrs:get_yaw , gps:num_sats , battery:voltage , rangefinder:distance_orient in meters; distance_cm_orient is deprecated , esc_telem:get_rpm , vehicle:get_mode , arming:is_armed ; actions: vehicle:set_mode , vehicle:set_target_velocity_NED , vehicle:set_target_location , mission:set_current_cmd , SRV_Channels:set_output_pwm , relay:on , param:set / param:add_param your own parameters with a prefix , gcs:send_text , logger:write your own log messages! , notify:play_tune , rc:get_aux_cached switch RCx_OPTION = 300..307 Scripting1..8 , serial:find_serial your own protocol on a UART , CAN:get_device DroneCAN , periph on AP_Periph. Timers — return update, 100 ms until the next call . Scripting parameters: SCR_ENABLE , SCR_HEAP_SIZE memory; F4 doesn't have enough → only H7/F7 with headroom , SCR_VM_I_COUNT instruction limit per call — protection against hangs , SCR_DEBUG_OPTS . Applets as a textbook libraries/AP_Scripting/applets/ — ready-made, with an .md description: motor_failure_test.lua stops motors per the MOT_STOP_BITMASK bitmask with the Scripting1 switch — a motor-failure test on a hexa/X8 in SITL and in the field , VTOL-quicktune.lua QuikTune for multicopters and VTOL , rover-quicktune.lua , copter-deadreckon-home.lua dead-reckoning return on GPS loss , arming-checks.lua your own pre-arm checks , ahrs-source-extnav-optflow.lua switching EKF sources by quality , BattEstimate.lua , MissionSelector.lua , net_webserver.lua , crsf-calibrate.lua , SmartAudio.lua . Reading them is the best way to learn the API and the style defensive checks, pcall -like wrappers, parameters via param:add_table . Worked example: ESC temperature guard lua -- esc_temp_guard.lua: warn at 80 C, switch to LAND at 100 C any ESC , check every 500 ms local WARN, CRIT = 80, 100 local MODE_LAND = 9 local warned = false function update for i = 0, 7 do local t = esc_telem:get_temperature i -- nil if no telemetry; value in centi-degrees if t then t = t // 100 if t = CRIT and arming:is_armed and vehicle:get_mode ~= MODE_LAND then gcs:send_text 2, string.format "ESC %d %dC: LAND", i + 1, t vehicle:set_mode MODE_LAND elseif t = WARN and not warned then gcs:send_text 4, string.format "ESC %d temp %dC", i + 1, t ; warned = true end end end return update, 500 end return update Testing in SITL: SIM_ESC_TELEM = 1 , temporarily set the threshold to 30 °C, make sure it triggers; then — on the test bench. Record it in the FMEA as a mitigation with a reference to the test the “Fault Tolerance” module . {{diagram:lua-runtime How a script runs: a file from APM/scripts/ goes into the Lua VM, update returns itself and the period, pcall catches errors, actions go through API bindings.}} practice Step 1. Enable scripting in SITL param set SCR_ENABLE 1 reboot Step 2. An indicator script on a switch A minimal script: reports Scripting2 switch position changes and the arming state to the GCS. lua -- switch_report.lua: report Scripting2 switch position and arming state to the GCS local SWITCH_OPTION = 301 -- RCx_OPTION = 301 Scripting2 local switch = rc:find_channel_for_option SWITCH_OPTION local last_pos = -1 function update if not switch then gcs:send_text 4, "switch_report: no channel with RCx_OPTION=301" return update, 5000 end local pos = switch:get_aux_switch_pos if pos ~= last_pos then local armed = arming:is_armed and "ARMED" or "disarmed" gcs:send_text 6, string.format "Scripting2 - %d %s ", pos, armed last_pos = pos end return update, 200 end return update, 1000 Put the file in scripts/ , assign a switch param set RC9_OPTION 301 , restart SITL, and flip the switch a few times. This module covers the coaxial X8 layout using a build on two Tarot Ironman 650 frames as the example, thr
headings: X8 (OctaQuad): pros and cons Example build Thrust and the throttle curve Vibration Fault tolerance Numbers for the course platform (X8, 2×Tarot 650, 4008 380KV, 15×5.5, 6S Li-Ion, ~6 kg) Motor failure: what the mixer does Operating a big vehicle Step 1. text: summary An eight-motor vehicle with 15–17" props is a different beast from a five-inch quad: slow motors, huge inertia, a low thrust-to-weight ratio, and the price of a mistake is an expensive payload. This module covers the coaxial X8 layout using a build on two Tarot Ironman 650 frames as the example, thrust and vibration setup in ArduPilot, and fault-tolerance testing before the first flight with a payload. theory X8 OctaQuad : pros and cons An X8 has four arms with two coaxial motors on each: upper and lower, spinning in opposite directions. - Pros: eight motors in a quadcopter footprint; a single motor failure does not bring the vehicle down; compact for transport. - Cons: the lower prop works in the upper prop's wash, so a coaxial pair gives less thrust than two separate props. A rule-of-thumb loss is around 15% it depends on the props and the spacing between them . In ArduPilot this is FRAME_CLASS = 4 OctaQuad and FRAME_TYPE = 1 X . Motor order and directions strictly follow the OctaQuad X diagram in the documentation. Example build The course's training platform: two Tarot Ironman 650 frames, 8 Tarot 4008 380KV motors, 8 Flycolor 45A ESCs, 6S Li-Ion power. Low KV and big props are a bet on efficiency and flight time, not on agility. Li-Ion was chosen because of the moderate current in hover. Thrust and the throttle curve - MOT_THST_HOVER — hover throttle; ArduPilot refines it by itself in flight. Altitude hold depends on it. - MOT_THST_EXPO — thrust linearization. Big props usually need a higher value than five-inch ones. - MOT_SPIN_ARM and MOT_SPIN_MIN — the spin when armed and the in-flight minimum: the motors should spin confidently but not lift the vehicle. - The motor protocol MOT_PWM_TYPE : DShot if the ESCs support it, otherwise PWM with ESC calibration. For starting values Mission Planner has the Initial Tune Parameters helper: it calculates the basic filters and limits from the prop size and voltage. Vibration Big slow props produce low-frequency vibration that is harder to filter. With vibration the EKF starts to “drift”: in the logs you see it as rising VIBE and accelerometer clipping, in flight as altitude loss or IMU failure messages. The cure, in order of priority: balancing props and motors, frame stiffness, flight controller damping, and only then filters. The harmonic notch filter INS_HNTCH_ tracks the motor speed from throttle or from ESC telemetry — the counterpart of the Betaflight RPM filter. Fault tolerance The main reason to go octo is to survive a motor failure. But you have to test that, not assume it: in SITL with the motor-failure applet the Lua module , then on the real vehicle at altitude and without a payload. Numbers for the course platform X8, 2×Tarot 650, 4008 380KV, 15×5.5, 6S Li-Ion, ~6 kg From the “Propeller Aerodynamics” module: hover ≈ 880 g of thrust per motor including coaxial losses, ~7 A per motor, 56 A for the pack; Li-Ion 6S 20 Ah → ~17 min of hover; MOT_THST_HOVER ≈ 0.3–0.35; MOT_THST_EXPO 0.65–0.7 15" ; INS_GYRO_FILTER ≈ 30 Hz between 40 Hz for 10" and 20 Hz for 20" ; ATC_RAT_ _FLTD 10; starting ATC_RAT_RLL_P/I 0.08, D 0.003, ATC_ANG_RLL_P 4.5; ATC_ACC_R/P_MAX ≈ 500–700 °/s² before 4.7 — ATC_ACCEL_R/P_MAX in cdeg/s², 50 000–70 000; slower than a 5" ; PSC_D_ACC_P before 4.7 — PSC_ACCZ_P ; in 4.7 the value is ×0.1 ≈ 0.3× the hover throttle. Arm wires 12 AWG, XT90 the “Redundancy” module . The fundamental motor harmonic in hover is ~55–65 Hz 3400–3900 rpm — INS_HNTCH_ from ESC telemetry, INS_HNTCH_HMNCS = 7 harmonics 1–3 up to 200 Hz , INS_HNTCH_FREQ at least 50. Motor failure: what the mixer does AP_MotorsMatrix::output_armed_stabilizing allocates roll/pitch, then yaw with a minimum headroom of MOT_YAW_HEADROOM , and throttle gets what is left within MOT_YAW_HEADROOM 200 by default, in PWM units of yaw headroom . When one X8 motor fails, its coaxial partner and the opposite pair take the load; visually — a slight sag and a rise in RCOU of the neighboring channels. Test: the motor_failure_test.lua applet MOT_STOP_BITMASK , the Scripting1 switch first in SITL -f octa-quad , then in the field at 20+ m altitude without a payload, with a spotter. Operating a big vehicle The pre-arm ritual gets longer: 8 props tightness, cracks , 8 ESCs heat after the previous flight , the Li-Ion balancer by group, a GPS fix up to 14+ satellites, the geofence, a 30 m radius area with no people, a buzzer and a sling for carrying. Any change in mass payload, battery → recompute MOT_THST_HOVER it will learn and check PSC_D_ACC_ before 4.7 — PSC_ACCZ_ . Logs — every flight; VIBE < 15 on big props is normal, 30 — go looking. {{diagram:x8-layout X8: four arms with coaxial pairs; on a motor failure the coaxial partner and the opposite pair take the load, and the throttle headroom in hover is your margin for a failure.}} practice Step 1. SITL first sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter -f octa-quad --console --map Practice takeoff, LOITER, RTL and a motor failure before you touch the hardware. Step 2. Configuring the real frame 1. FRAME_CLASS = 4 , FRAME_TYPE = 1 , reboot. 2. With props off — Motor Test on each motor: order and direction per the OctaQuad X diagram. 3. ESC calibration for PWM or choosing DShot. 4. Initial Tune Parameters for the prop size and cell count. 5. Check: all props are the same model, correct direction and tightness. Step 3. First flights 1. A low hover in STABILIZE, then ALT_HOLD, with logging. 2. Log analysis: VIBE vibration and clipping , the real hover throttle, current and battery sag. 3. Only then AUTOTUNE — one axis at a time, in calm weather. 4. The motor failure test — at altitude, without a payload, ready to take over control. What you should end up with and what to record - SITL. The octa-quad frame in SITL is the same OctaQuad: eight motors, four coaxial pairs. A single motor failure SIM_ENGINE_FAIL — the motor mask, SIM_ENGINE_MUL = 0 is survivable on an octo: the vehicle rolls, the remaining motors make up the thrust, the position holds.

title: Wing aerodynamics and plane flight modes
summary: A wing flies differently: lift depends on the square of airspeed, it has a stall speed, the CG decides whether it is stable at all, and the autopilot does not control “altitude” and “speed” separately but energy (TECS). This module gives you the calculations to do before the first hand launch: lift
headings: Lift CG and stability Control surfaces and modes TECS: energy control Launch and landing Step 1. Wing calculation Step 2. CG Step 3. Parameters Step 4. Checking against flight Worked calculation for self-check What you should end up with and what to record
text: summary A wing flies differently: lift depends on the square of airspeed, it has a stall speed, the CG decides whether it is stable at all, and the autopilot does not control “altitude” and “speed” separately but energy TECS . This module gives you the calculations to do before the first hand launch: lift and wing loading, stall and cruise speed, CG position and static margin — and ties them to the ArduPlane parameters ARSPD_ , TECS_ , AIRSPEED_CRUISE/MIN/MAX , TRIM_ and INAV ones nav_fw_ , fw_ . theory Lift L = ½ · ρ · V² · S · C_L — air density, airspeed squared, wing area, lift coefficient depends on the angle of attack α and the airfoil; it grows roughly linearly up to the critical angle of 10–15°, then comes the stall . In level flight L = m·g. - Wing loading W/S g/dm² or N/m² : the higher it is, the faster you have to fly, and the worse the wing does in thermals and on landing. 1–1.5 m FPV wings: 30–60 g/dm²; mapping planes: 40–80; foam trainers: 20–35. - Stall speed : V_s = √ 2·m·g / ρ·S·C_Lmax . C_Lmax for simple airfoils without high-lift devices is 1.0–1.3. Example: m = 1.8 kg, S = 0.35 m², C_Lmax = 1.1 → V_s = √ 2·1.8·9.81/ 1.225·0.35·1.1 ≈ 8.7 m/s. In a turn with bank angle φ the lift has to be larger: V_s φ = V_s/√cos φ — at 60° of bank the stall speed is 41% higher. - Cruise : 1.3–1.6 V_s for economy the best L/D is usually near 1.3 V_s , 2 V_s and above for speed/wind. The minimum safe airspeed in the autopilot is ≥ 1.2–1.3 V_s. - Drag D = ½ρV²·S·C_D; C_D = C_D0 + k·C_L² parasitic + induced . At low speed induced drag dominates grows as 1/V² , at high speed parasitic drag does V² . Minimum power is at a speed slightly below the minimum-drag speed: hence “fly slower than it feels” for endurance. CG and stability A wing is stable in pitch if the center of gravity CG is ahead of the neutral point the aerodynamic center of the whole aircraft . Static margin = x_np − x_cg /MAC mean aerodynamic chord — 5–15% is normal; 0 is neutral it flies but does not return by itself ; negative is unstable the autopilot will not save you when the control surfaces saturate . For a flying wing no tailplane the neutral point is ≈ 25% MAC quarter chord with corrections for sweep; the CG is set at 15–20% MAC. Online wing CG calculators from span, root/tip chord and sweep do exactly this calculation. An aft CG means sharp, “twitchy” responses and a tendency to spin; a forward CG means a heavy nose, high landing speed and lots of up elevator. Ground check: balance it on your fingertips/stands at the calculated point with the battery and all the payload. Flight check: the “dive test” — from level flight, let go of the sticks in a shallow dive: the plane pulls out to level by itself forward CG — sharply; aft CG — it keeps diving/tucks in . Control surfaces and modes Elevons on a wing mix elevator and ailerons; a conventional plane has separate surfaces. The autopilot stabilizes roll and pitch FBWA , holds altitude and heading FBWB , CRUISE , flies waypoints AUTO , returns home RTL , lands AUTOLAND / LAND . Without an airspeed sensor the autopilot estimates airspeed from GPS and wind — worse in wind; with a pitot tube ARSPD_TYPE , calibration ARSPD_AUTOCAL , ARSPD_RATIO it is accurate. TECS: energy control The total energy of the plane = potential altitude + kinetic speed . Throttle changes the sum of the energy, the elevator changes the split between altitude and speed. TECS Total Energy Control System controls it exactly that way: TECS_CLMB_MAX max climb, m/s at full throttle , TECS_SINK_MIN sink at idle , TECS_SINK_MAX , TECS_TIME_CONST , TECS_SPDWEIGHT 0 — hold altitude at the cost of speed, 2 — hold speed at the cost of altitude; 1 — balance, the default; 2 — pitch holds speed only, throttle holds altitude, recommended for gliders , TECS_PTCH_DAMP , TECS_THR_DAMP . Speeds: AIRSPEED_MIN ≥ 1.2 V_s , AIRSPEED_CRUISE , AIRSPEED_MAX , TRIM_THROTTLE cruise throttle , THR_MIN/MAX . AIRSPEED_STALL is used for warnings/protection. INAV: nav_fw_cruise_speed , nav_fw_min_thr/max_thr/cruise_thr , nav_fw_climb_angle/dive_angle , fw_min_throttle_down_pitch — simpler, no energy model, but the same idea: throttle for climb, pitch for speed. Launch and landing Hand launch/catapult: TKOFF_THR_MINACC launch detection by acceleration , TKOFF_THR_DELAY , TKOFF_LVL_ALT ; INAV — autolaunch nav_fw_launch_ . Landing: glide slope LAND_PITCH_DEG , LAND_FLARE_ALT/SEC , a rangefinder for the flare; a wing lands on its belly into the wind at 1.1–1.2 V_s. {{diagram:tecs-energy TECS: the total energy error altitude + speed is closed with throttle, the error in their balance with pitch; that is why climbing without throttle headroom eats your airspeed.}} practice Step 1. Wing calculation Measure the span, root and tip chords, sweep; calculate S, MAC, wing loading, V_s C_Lmax 1.1 for an airfoil without high-lift devices , cruise at 1.4 V_s, V_s in a 45° bank. Step 2. CG Find the neutral point a wing calculator, or 25% MAC for a conventional plane ignoring the tailplane — with it the formula gets more complex, use a calculator , pick a 10% margin, mark the CG point, balance it with the battery. Write down the mass, CG and margin. Step 3. Parameters ArduPlane: AIRSPEED_MIN/CRUISE/MAX , starting TECS_ , TRIM_THROTTLE , ARSPD_ if you have a pitot tube. INAV: nav_fw_ . Justify every number with the calculation from step 1. Step 4. Checking against flight First flight in FBWA at altitude: slowly bleed off speed until the stall begins wobbling, nose drop — write down the speed from airspeed/GPS; compare it with the calculated V_s the difference is usually 10–20% because of C_Lmax and measurement errors . Dive test for the CG. Log: TECS , ARSP , CTUN.NavPitch . Worked calculation for self-check A wing with an area of 0.4 m², takeoff mass 2 kg: wing loading 5 kg/m². title: QuadPlane and tilt-rotor VTOL
summary: A tilt-rotor VTOL takes off like a multirotor and flies like a plane, tilting its motors on the fly. It's one of the most complex ArduPilot platforms: a copter mixer, a plane mixer and the tilt mechanics all live in one aircraft. This module is written at an experienced-pilot level and walks through
headings: QuadPlane tiltrotor configuration Output functions The main trap: a motor on a servo channel Case study: HeeWing T1 Ranger Transitions: the parameters that determine safety Worked example: the first transition Bring-up protocol (props off!) First flight What you should get and what to write down
text: summary A tilt-rotor VTOL takes off like a multirotor and flies like a plane, tilting its motors on the fly. It's one of the most complex ArduPilot platforms: a copter mixer, a plane mixer and the tilt mechanics all live in one aircraft. This module is written at an experienced-pilot level and walks through a real from-scratch bring-up of the HeeWing T1 Ranger tricopter wing: output assignment, an incident with a motor that spun up on its own, the limitations of the F405, and checking the transition on the ground. theory QuadPlane tiltrotor configuration - Q_ENABLE = 1 — enables the VTOL part in ArduPlane. After changing Q_ENABLE , Q_FRAME_CLASS , Q_FRAME_TYPE — reboot. - Q_FRAME_CLASS = 7 — tricopter. - Q_TILT_TYPE : 0 — continuous regular tilt servos , 1 — binary only “up/forward” , 2 — vectored yaw the left and right motors tilt independently and provide yaw in hover , 3 — bicopter. - Q_TILT_MASK — which motors tilt bit 0 — motor 1 . A tricopter with two tilting front motors — 3. - Q_TILT_MAX — the tilt angle while waiting for transition airspeed the default 45° suits most . - Q_TILT_RATE_UP / Q_TILT_RATE_DN — the tilt rate, °/s; a reasonable start is about 15°/s. - Q_TILT_YAW_ANGLE — for vectored yaw: how far the motors can go beyond 90°. Output functions Each output SERVOn_FUNCTION is assigned a role: - tricopter motors: Motor1 33 , Motor2 34 , Motor4 36 ; - tilt servos for vectored yaw: TiltMotorFrontLeft 75 , TiltMotorFrontRight 76 ; for regular tilt — TiltMotorsFront 41 ; - surfaces: Elevator 19 , FlaperonLeft 24 , FlaperonRight 25 . Check the function numbers against the documentation for your version: the table grows, but old numbers don't change. The main trap: a motor on a servo channel The flight controller's outputs are grouped by timers. Within a group all outputs share one protocol and rate: you can't have DShot for a motor and 50 Hz for a servo on the same timer. If the physical wiring doesn't match the assigned functions, you get one of two things: a servo receives “throttle” and slams into its stop, or an ESC receives a servo signal — and the motor spins up without a command. Case study: HeeWing T1 Ranger Configuration: the stock HeeWing F405, a tilt tricopter — the two front motors tilt, the rear one is fixed. Project requirements: arm only from a radio switch, GPS not required for arming and basic flight. The incident. While checking channels, one motor unexpectedly spun up to full. Cause: a category mismatch — motor functions were assigned to outputs physically connected to servos, and vice versa. The project was halted until a full recheck. How it was sorted out. With props off, by hand, one output at a time, an “output → device” map was built and checked against the list of 8 devices: 1. elevator; 2. left flaperon; 3. right flaperon; 4. left nacelle tilt servo; 5. right nacelle tilt servo; 6. left tilting motor; 7. right tilting motor; 8. rear fixed motor. After that the functions were reassigned on all 8 channels, and the motors and servos were split into timer groups with compatible protocols. Hardware limitations. The F405 has no Lua scripting, and some features are cut down. This build has no compass at all, and the GPS was unstable at the time of setup. So EKF3 was disabled and DCM attitude estimation was chosen: the aircraft arms and flies without GPS and a compass, but without altitude and position hold. The set of modes for this decision: MANUAL, FBWA, ACRO, QSTABILIZE for takeoff, QLAND for landing. This is a deliberate compromise for specific hardware, not a default recommendation. Transitions: the parameters that determine safety - Forward VTOL → wing : in wing modes with Q_ENABLE the aircraft is held up by the VTOL motors until airspeed reaches AIRSPEED_MIN the minimum wing airspeed; before 4.5 — ARSPD_FBW_MIN or Q_TRANSITION_MS elapses ms; without an airspeed sensor — by time ; the tilt motors tilt at Q_TILT_RATE_UP . An AIRSPEED_MIN too small relative to V_s the “Wing Aerodynamics” module = a stall right after the transition. - Back wing → VTOL : when switching to Q modes the VTOL motors turn on immediately; Q_TRANS_DECEL m/s² sets the deceleration; Q_ASSIST_SPEED m/s — below this airspeed in plane modes the VTOL motors help automatically assist — stall protection; Q_ASSIST_ANGLE , Q_ASSIST_ALT — assist at a large bank angle / at low altitude. - VTOL loop : Q_A_RAT_ VTOL rate PID , Q_A_ANG_ , Q_P_ position , Q_M_THST_HOVER , Q_M_SPIN_MIN/ARM , Q_WVANE_ weathervaning into the wind . QAUTOTUNE — for the VTOL part; TECS and PTCH2SRV_ / RLL2SRV_ — for the wing. - Landing : Q_LAND_FINAL_SPD m/s , Q_LAND_FINAL_ALT ; RTL as VTOL Q_RTL_MODE or plane-style with a transition to QLAND near home. {{diagram:quadplane-transition VTOL → wing transition: the VTOL motors hold the aircraft until AIRSPEED_MIN is reached or Q_TRANSITION_MS expires.}} Worked example: the first transition Order: 1 QSTABILIZE/QHOVER hover and QLOITER GPS — the VTOL part is tuned; 2 FBWA/MANUAL checked separately with a toss or hand launch, if the design allows; 3 a transition at an altitude of ≥ 60 m in FBWA with AIRSPEED_MIN = 1.3 V_s, Q_ASSIST_SPEED = 1.2 V_s, Q_TRANSITION_MS 5000; watch airspeed ARSP , tilt RCOU , altitude; 4 a back transition to QHOVER; log → QTUN VTOL , TECS , ATT . Without an airspeed sensor, a time-based transition is only for flying over an open field with an altitude margin. practice Bring-up protocol props off! 1. Save the parameters to a file. 2. Build the “output → physical device” map by hand, one output at a time. 3. Assign SERVOn_FUNCTION per the map. Split the motors and servos into timer groups with compatible protocols. 4. Q_ENABLE , Q_FRAME_CLASS , Q_TILT_ — reboot. 5. Check servo directions SERVOn_REVERSED : in MANUAL the motors point forward, in QSTABILIZE — up. 6. On the ground, switch MANUAL ↔ QSTABILIZE and check that the tilt is smooth and the servos are trimmed. 7. Check the response of the surfaces and the tilt to roll, pitch and yaw in both mode

title: ArduPilot tuning: AUTOTUNE, filters, ESC-based notch
summary: Tuning ArduCopter isn't “run AUTOTUNE” — it's seven steps in the right order: parameters for the vehicle size → first stable flight → assessment → harmonic notch on motor noise → manual/QuikTune roll-pitch → AUTOTUNE axis by axis → input shaping for feel. This module walks through them with paramete

Input shaping What to check afterwards Step 1. SITL Step 2. Notch in the field Step 3. QuikTune/manual Step 4. AUTOTUNE in the field What you should get and what to record
text: summary Tuning ArduCopter isn't “run AUTOTUNE” — it's seven steps in the right order: parameters for the vehicle size → first stable flight → assessment → harmonic notch on motor noise → manual/QuikTune roll-pitch → AUTOTUNE axis by axis → input shaping for feel. This module walks through them with parameters and log checks ATT , RATE , VIBE , spectra from batch sampling/raw IMU , explains what AUTOTUNE does internally and why it needs noise below a threshold , and how to set up a notch tracking ESC telemetry or throttle. The lab is in SITL and in the field. theory Step 1. Parameters before the first flight Starting values depend on prop size the “Setting the Aircraft Up for Tuning” document : INS_GYRO_FILTER 80 Hz for 5", 40 for 10", 20 for 20" and larger , ATC_RAT_ _FLTD/FLTE/FLTT D/E/T rate filters — half of the gyro filter for D , MOT_THST_EXPO 0.65 for 10", 0.55–0.6 for 5" , MOT_SPIN_ARM/MIN , MOT_THST_HOVER it will learn, MOT_HOVER_LEARN = 2 , ATC_THR_MIX_MAN , PSC_D_ACC_P/I before 4.7 — PSC_ACCZ_P/I , in 4.7 the values are ×0.1 for the hover throttle, ATC_INPUT_TC stick feel . For large/heavy vehicles — reduced initial PIDs ATC_RAT_RLL_P/I 0.05–0.1 instead of 0.135, D 0.002–0.004 . Steps 2–3. First flight and assessment Stabilize/AltHold at minimum weight, full battery “most agile configuration” . In the log: RATE.RDes vs RATE.R requested vs actual — tracking without oscillations; ATT.DesRoll vs ATT.Roll ; VIBE.VibeX/Y/Z < 15–30 m/s², Clip = 0; CTUN.ThO hover throttle, learned MOT_THST_HOVER 0.2–0.5 . Oscillations right away → lower P/D by 30–50%, don't keep flying. Step 4. Harmonic notch Motor noise gets into the D-term and heats the motors; a low-frequency LPF adds latency the “Signals and spectra” module . A notch cuts only the motor frequencies: 1. Find the frequency : batch sampling INS_LOG_BAT_MASK = 1 — first IMU; INS_LOG_BAT_OPT : 0 — raw data before the filters, 2 — after the filters, 4 — before and after at 1 kHz or, on H7 with 4.5+, raw IMU logging INS_RAW_LOG_OPT ; fly a hover + gentle maneuvers; spectrum in MAVExplorer/Filter Review Tool/your own Python. 2. Enable : INS_HNTCH_ENABLE = 1 , reboot. 3. Mode INS_HNTCH_MODE : 3 — ESC telemetry the best, tracks each motor, needs ESC telemetry or BLHeli bidir DShot ; 1 — throttle-based INS_HNTCH_REF = hover throttle, INS_HNTCH_FREQ — the frequency at hover, scaled by √ throttle/ref ; change REF when the payload changes ; 4 — in-flight FFT F7/H7, one filter ; 0 — static. 4. Bandwidth and depth : INS_HNTCH_BW ≈ half of FREQ for throttle mode, narrower for ESC , INS_HNTCH_ATT 40 dB typical , INS_HNTCH_HMNCS harmonics bitmask: 3 = 1st and 2nd, 7 = 1st–3rd; “three harmonics is usually safe” , INS_HNTCH_OPTS bit 1 — multi-source, per motor; bit 2 — update at loop rate with bidir DShot; bit 5 — fall back to the minimum frequency on RPM loss; don't combine bits 0 and 4 double/triple — with both set, only double works . 5. Verify : a log with batch sampling after the filters INS_LOG_BAT_OPT = 2 , the motor peaks should drop by 20+ dB; the second set INS_HNTC2_ is for frame resonance static . Step 5. Manual roll/pitch or QuikTune Mandatory before AUTOTUNE: AUTOTUNE starts from the current values and aborts on noise. QuikTune the Lua applet VTOL-quicktune.lua , enabled with the QUIK_ENABLE parameter, switch — RCx_OPTION = 300 or QUIK_RC_FUNC raises P/D until the first oscillation and backs off by QUIK_GAIN_MARGIN %. Manually: D until it oscillates → −30%, P until it oscillates → −30%, I = P. Step 6. AUTOTUNE What it does: in AltHold/Loiter it applies a series of short “kicks” on one axis twitches , measures the response and looks for the maximum rate D, then rate P I = P , then angle P, aiming for the target overshoot. Parameters: AUTOTUNE_AXES bitmask: 1 roll, 2 pitch, 4 yaw, 8 yaw-D; on large vehicles it's better to do one axis per flight , AUTOTUNE_AGGR 0.05–0.10, default 0.075 since 4.6 0.1 in 4.5 and earlier ; higher — more aggressive and more noise-tolerant, lower — more responsive , AUTOTUNE_MIN_D lower limit for D — so it doesn't drop to zero on a noisy vehicle . Conditions: wind < 3 m/s, 20+ m of altitude and space, full battery, notch configured. The result is saved only when you disarm with the switch on / in AUTOTUNE mode message “Saved gains for …” ; RCx_OPTION = 180 lets you switch between the old and new gains to compare. The ATUN log overview and ATDE details of each twitch show where it stopped; the GCS messages “Twitch”, “success 1/4” are in the log too. Sign of success: the final ATC_RAT_ _D are above AUTOTUNE_MIN_D . Step 7. Input shaping ATC_INPUT_TC 0.15 smooth → 0.05 crisp , ATC_ACC_R/P/Y_MAX °/s²; before 4.7 — ATC_ACCEL_R/P/Y_MAX in cdeg/s² , ATC_RATE_R/P/Y_MAX , ATC_ANG_ _P AUTOTUNE sets them, you can soften them . This isn't stability — it's feel. What to check afterwards RATE.RDes/R — response without overshoot 10%; RATE.ROut PID output without saturation; VIBE hasn't gone up; motor temperature; the post-filter spectrum is clean; PIDR.P/I/D per-axis PID logging with PID enabled in LOG_BITMASK — the share of D noise. {{diagram:ap-tuning-order Tuning order: base parameters → harmonic notch → QuikTune or manual tuning → AUTOTUNE → input shaping, with a log after every step.}} practice Step 1. SITL sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter -f quad : set the starting parameters for 10", AUTOTUNE roll AUTOTUNE_AXES = 1 in AltHold; look at ATUN in the log and the final ATC_RAT_RLL_ . Repeat with AUTOTUNE_AGGR = 0.05 — compare. Step 2. Notch in the field Batch sampling before the filters → spectrum → hover frequency → INS_HNTCH_ ESC mode if you have telemetry → batch after the filters → before/after spectrum with numbers in dB. Step 3. QuikTune/manual Roll-pitch up to the first oscillation, back off; check with the RATE log. Step 4. AUTOTUNE in the field One axis per flight; save; a control flight with a log; compare RATE.RDes/R before/after. What you should get and what to record - Step 1 SITL . AUTOTUNE is enabled with a switch

Here is the order of setting up a plane in ArduPlane, which decides whether AUTO holds altitude and the line or oscillates: preparation (control surfaces, CG, airspeeds), in-flight AUT
headings: Order is everything Preparation before the first tuning Roll and pitch AUTOTUNE TECS from test flights L1 navigation Automatic landing PX4: the same stages Step 1. A SITL plane Step 2. AUTOTUNE Step 3. TECS Step 4. L1 Step 5. Landing (SITL)
text: summary “Wing Aerodynamics” explained why a plane flies and what TECS is; “ArduPilot Tuning” covered how a copter is tuned. Here is the order of setting up a plane in ArduPlane, which decides whether AUTO holds altitude and the line or oscillates: preparation control surfaces, CG, airspeeds , in-flight AUTOTUNE of roll and pitch, TECS from test flights with concrete numbers, the L1 navigation controller on a rectangular mission, and automatic landing with a flare. PX4 equivalents are given at the end — the names differ there including NPFG navigation , but the logic is the same. theory Order is everything Inner loops before outer ones: roll and pitch control surfaces → angles → TECS altitude and airspeed via throttle and pitch → navigation the path line via roll → landing. A poorly tuned pitch looks like “TECS is oscillating altitude,” and a bad roll looks like “L1 is weaving.” Starting from the outer loop means fixing the symptom. Preparation before the first tuning - Control surfaces and reversals. In FBWA, tilt the plane by hand: the ailerons and elevator must counteract the tilt. In MANUAL the sticks must move the surfaces the right way. A mistake here means a crash on the very first hand launch in a stabilized mode. - CG — per the calculation from “Wing Aerodynamics”; slightly nose-heavy is safer. - Airspeeds Plane 4.5+, m/s : AIRSPEED_MIN ≥ ~1.2 × stall speed , AIRSPEED_CRUISE , AIRSPEED_MAX ; SCALING_SPEED — the typical cruise speed; set it before tuning and don't touch it afterward: the gains are scaled from it. - Control surface limits. RLL2SRV_RMAX , PTCH2SRV_RMAX_UP/DN — the maximum rates the plane can actually achieve; RLL_RATE_SMAX , PTCH_RATE_SMAX — matched to the servo speed. - Trimming. In FBWA in level flight — SERVO_AUTO_TRIM = 1 or manual trims; PTCH_TRIM_DEG — the pitch angle of level flight. - Return point rally and verified failsafes. Roll and pitch AUTOTUNE - Enabling: the AUTOTUNE mode on the mode switch, or a switch with RCx_OPTION = 107 in FBWA/FBWB/CRUISE. - AUTOTUNE_LEVEL — the target aggressiveness: 6 by default 75 °/s . Slow large wings and gliders — 2–3; above 7 — only after tuning at a lower level. - AUTOTUNE_AXES — which axes to tune; yaw — only with YAW_RATE_ENABLE = 1 . - Maneuvers: sharp stick reversals with a short pause at the end point, one axis at a time; learning happens only when the requested rate is large enough. Without telemetry — at least 20 reversals per axis, more is better, until the completion message. - Saving: P and D are written when an axis finishes, FF and I — when you exit the mode. Exit mid-axis — that axis gets its old values back. RCx_OPTION = 180 — a switch to compare the old and new gains. - Result: RLL_RATE_FF/P/I/D , PTCH_RATE_FF/P/I/D , and the angle → rate relationship via the time constants RLL2SRV_TCONST and PTCH2SRV_TCONST 0.5 s by default : within τ the plane covers ~63 % of the requested angle. {{diagram:chart-plane-tconst Roll response to a 30° step at different time constants: smaller τ — a sharper response, larger — softer; 0.5 s by default.}} TECS from test flights TECS is tuned after pitch. The starting values are measured in FBWA, not guessed: 1. THR_MAX — so that at cruise the plane climbs at PTCH_LIM_MAX_DEG . 2. TRIM_THROTTLE — the throttle for level flight at cruise. 3. PTCH_LIM_MAX_DEG — full throttle, maximum pitch: airspeed should stay near cruise. If it rises — raise the limit or lower THR_MAX ; if it drops below AIRSPEED_MIN — the opposite. 4. TECS_CLMB_MAX — the real climb rate at THR_MAX for electric planes — measure at the end of the battery . 5. TECS_SINK_MIN — the sink rate at idle at cruise airspeed; TECS_SINK_MAX — the fastest descent without exceeding PTCH_LIM_MIN_DEG and AIRSPEED_MAX . Check in LOITER/AUTO: altitude holds within ~10 m with no noticeable pitch oscillation; if it oscillates — TECS_TIME_CONST +1. A 50 m climb command: throttle around 80 % of THR_MAX , airspeed holds, pitch ~5° below the limit. If it hits THR_MAX and loses airspeed — lower TECS_CLMB_MAX . Oscillations — TECS_PTCH_DAMP in steps of 0.1 no higher than 0.5 without a noise analysis , then TECS_TIME_CONST again. Fine tuning: TECS_SPDWEIGHT 0 — altitude priority, 1 — balance, 2 — airspeed, for gliders , TECS_RLL2THR — compensation for energy loss in a turn. L1 navigation The L1 controller turns deviation from the line into a roll command. NAVL1_PERIOD — the period of “how sharply to return to the line” in seconds: smaller is sharper. NAVL1_DAMPING — damping 0.75 by default; don't drop it noticeably below 0.6 . - ROLL_LIMIT_DEG — the bank the plane holds without stalling ~50° for slow gliders, ~65° for aerobatic planes . - A rectangular mission within line of sight, WP_RADIUS — about two seconds of flight at cruise. - Turns are sluggish, the plane overshoots the line — NAVL1_PERIOD −5; it weaves after a turn — +1…2. Then adjust NAVL1_DAMPING in steps of 0.05. Automatic landing The mission ends with NAV_LAND with an approach into the wind. Key parameters: LAND_FLARE_ALT the altitude where the flare starts , LAND_FLARE_SEC how many seconds before touchdown , TECS_LAND_ARSPD approach airspeed , TECS_LAND_SINK sink rate on the glide slope , LAND_PITCH_DEG pitch during the flare . Without a lidar, altitude comes from the barometer, and an error of a few meters is common: a rangefinder for landing RNGFND_LANDING = 1 turns a lottery into a repeatable procedure. The first approaches — with an abort go-around at a safe altitude. PX4: the same stages Roll and pitch — FW_RR_ , FW_PR_ and the fixed-wing autotune; TECS — FW_T_ FW_T_CLMB_MAX , FW_T_SINK_MIN , FW_T_SINK_MAX and others ; navigation — NPFG NPFG_PERIOD , NPFG_DAMPING , the same idea as L1; landing — FW_LND_ . The parameter set depends on the version — check against the Fixed-wing tuning page for your version. practice Step 1. A SITL plane sim_vehicle.py -v ArduPlane --map --console . Take off in AUTO with the standard mission, switch to FBWA, check that the control surfaces

This module treats them as a system: what exactly triggers, in what order, and how they interact (for example, a low
headings: ArduCopter failsafe map How they interact Flight FMEA What you can and should verify in SITL Lua as the last line of defense Step 1. Configure Step 2. FMEA Step 3. SITL tests Step 4. Field check
text: summary ArduPilot has seven independent failsafes radio, GCS, battery, EKF, dead reckoning, vibration, geofence plus pre-arm checks, and each one has an action, a threshold and exceptions. This module treats them as a system: what exactly triggers, in what order, and how they interact for example, a low battery during an RTL triggered by radio loss ; how to run an FMEA of your own platform failure → how you notice it → what to do → how to verify ; and how to verify every scenario in SITL before you fly . The lab is an FMEA table with 10+ failures and a test log. theory ArduCopter failsafe map Failsafe Trigger Parameters Actions values --- --- --- --- Radio RC the receiver stopped outputting frames no pulses or the throttle channel ≤ FS_THR_VALUE PWM, 910–1100 FS_THR_ENABLE , FS_THR_VALUE 0 off, 1 RTL, 3 Land, 4 SmartRTL/RTL, 5 SmartRTL/Land, 6 DO_LAND_START or RTL, 7 Brake/Land GCS no heartbeat from the ground station for FS_GCS_TIMEOUT 5 s by default FS_GCS_ENABLE , FS_GCS_TIMEOUT 0 off, 1 RTL, 3 SmartRTL/RTL, 4 SmartRTL/Land, 5 Land, 6 DO_LAND_START or RTL, 7 Brake/Land numbering differs from FS_THR_ENABLE ; relevant for Guided/telemetry Battery low voltage < BATT_LOW_VOLT with the BATT_LOW_TIMER timer or remaining capacity < BATT_LOW_MAH BATT_FS_LOW_ACT 0 warning, 1 Land, 2 RTL, 3 SmartRTL/RTL, 4 SmartRTL/Land, 5 Terminate, 6 DO_LAND_START/RTL, 7 Brake/Land Battery critical < BATT_CRT_VOLT / BATT_CRT_MAH BATT_FS_CRT_ACT the same, usually Land EKF variances FS_EKF_THRESH FS_EKF_ACTION 0 message, 1 Land if the mode requires position, 2 AltHold, 3 Land always Dead reckoning the EKF lost its position/velocity sources and is running on wind estimates FS_DR_ENABLE , FS_DR_TIMEOUT Land / RTL / SmartRTL… Vibration accelerometer clipping, altitude error FS_VIBE_ENABLE modified altitude estimation and control Geofence leaving the circle/polygon/altitude limit FENCE_ENABLE , FENCE_TYPE , FENCE_ACTION , FENCE_ALT_MAX , FENCE_RADIUS , FENCE_MARGIN 0 message, 1 RTL/Land, 2 Land always, 3 SmartRTL/RTL, 4 Brake/Land, 5 SmartRTL/Land Options what to do instead of the default action FS_OPTIONS bitmask continue Auto on RC loss bit 0 , continue Auto on GCS loss bit 1 , Guided on RC loss bit 2 , continue landing bit 3 , pilot-controlled modes on GCS loss bit 4 Plus the pre-arm checks ARMING_SKIPCHK in 4.7+, ARMING_CHECK before that : compass, GPS, INS, parameters, voltage, geofence — disable them one at a time and only when you understand why. How they interact - Priority: critical battery overrides everything Land ; a low battery during a radio-loss RTL triggers the battery action usually RTL as well, but it can be Land — set it deliberately . - RTL requires position: during an EKF failsafe the action degrades to Land/AltHold. - RTL first climbs to RTL_ALT_M in 4.6 and earlier — RTL_ALT in cm; the minimum altitude above home for the return, 15 m by default; if the vehicle is already higher, it returns at its current altitude , flies home, loiters for RTL_LOIT_TIME , and lands RTL_ALT_FINAL = 0 . Obstacles taller than RTL_ALT_M mean a collision; the altitude geofence is yet another limiter. - SmartRTL returns along the path it flew stored points, SRTL_POINTS — good in a forest or between buildings, but it needs the point memory not to overflow. - Geofence: on a breach — the action; FENCE_MARGIN and an early warning; the pre-arm check won't let you arm outside the fence. - FS_OPTIONS “continue Auto on RC loss” is for BVLOS missions with an authorization; without one, keep it off. Flight FMEA FMEA Failure Mode and Effects Analysis is a table: failure → effect → how to detect it → severity 1–5 → probability 1–5 → detectability 1–5 → RPN = S·P·D → mitigation → verification . Mitigations: redundancy see the redundancy module , a failsafe action, a procedure checklist , a limit geofence, altitude , pilot training. A minimum failure list for a copter: RC loss; GCS loss; low battery; GPS degradation; compass fault; motor/ESC failure; BEC failure/FC reboot; vibration/clipping; parameter error after an update; wind above the design limit; video loss FPV ; pilot error wrong mode ; collision with an obstacle during RTL; SmartRTL overflow; rangefinder failure during terrain following. What you can and should verify in SITL Everything listed above except the mechanics: SITL supports SIM_RC_FAIL RC loss , GCS disconnection just close it , SIM_BATT_VOLTAGE voltage , SIM_GPS1_ENABLE , SIM_MAG1_OFS_ , SIM_ENGINE_FAIL , SIM_WIND_SPD/DIR , and the geofence set up the same way as in real life . Every test gets a log and a record: trigger, reaction time, action, outcome. Lua as the last line of defense A script can watch conditions the standard failsafes don't cover ESC temperature, disagreement between two GPS units, a mission timer and act on them vehicle:set_mode , a message, DO_LAND . It is an addition, not a replacement: the script itself can crash — hence SCR_HEAP_SIZE , error handling and a SITL test. {{diagram:failsafe-map ArduCopter failsafe map: event → parameter → typical action.}} practice Step 1. Configure Write down every parameter from the table for your vehicle with a justification: why RTL and not Land; why BATT_LOW_VOLT has exactly that value sag under load + a margin for an RTL from the geofence distance ; RTL_ALT_M above the obstacles at your field; geofence radius/altitude per the regulations; FS_OPTIONS = 0 without a BVLOS authorization. Step 2. FMEA A table of ≥ 10 failures following the template, with RPN; for every RPN above the threshold — a mitigation. Put it in your engineering folder. Step 3. SITL tests For each failsafe: scenario → expected → observed → log. Mandatory: RC loss in Loiter and in Auto; GCS loss in Guided; low battery during RTL; EKF failsafe on GPS loss; altitude and radius geofence; motor failure on a hexa/X8 if that is your platform . Step 4. Field check Only after SITL: RC failsafe on the ground with props off turn off the transmitter → motors disarm/message , then at 5 m altitude

title: Companion: why, and where the boundary is
summary: The flight controller does one thing: it keeps the aircraft in the air and executes simple commands, thousands of times per second and with no right to hang. Everything heavier — computer vision, planning, network connectivity, your own mission logic — lives on the companion computer. This module dr
headings: Separation of responsibilities How they communicate The “advises, doesn't control” rule Typical platforms Protocols and roles MAVLink routing Latency and what you can delegate to the companion Power, heat, failure Three typical architectures Choosing a platform for the task Architecture checklist before a project The observer code and what you should get Lab
text: summary The flight controller does one thing: it keeps the aircraft in the air and executes simple commands, thousands of times per second and with no right to hang. Everything heavier — computer vision, planning, network connectivity, your own mission logic — lives on the companion computer. This module draws the boundary between them, shows typical configurations from the ESP32 to the Jetson, and explains the main rule: the companion advises, the FC decides. theory Separation of responsibilities - Flight controller FC : stabilization, navigation, failsafe, mixer. Hard real time, minimal latency, proven code. It must keep flying even if the companion has hung, rebooted or burned out. - Companion: everything else. Vision, neural networks, map processing, complex scenarios, the internet, logging to the cloud, the operator interface. {{diagram:companion-system Companion and flight controller: the FC keeps the aircraft in the air, the companion sees, plans and talks to the network.}} The boundary follows the reliability requirement: whatever the aircraft would crash without goes on the FC; whatever it would just return home without goes on the companion. How they communicate Via MAVLink over UART the FC telemetry port or over a network. The companion is a separate component in the same MAVLink system. It can: - read telemetry and parameters; - switch the aircraft to GUIDED and set position/velocity targets; - upload and start missions; - receive text messages and status. What it doesn't do: it doesn't control the motors directly and doesn't replace stabilization. Even with offboard control, the FC itself watches the limits and the failsafe. The “advises, doesn't control” rule The companion proposes “fly to point X at speed Y”. The FC checks the geofence, the battery, the EKF health and executes — or refuses. If the companion stops sending commands, the FC switches to a safe mode on a timeout. That is exactly why the GCS failsafe and GUIDED timeouts are part of the design, not a nuisance. Typical platforms - ESP32 / ESP32-S3 — a microcontroller with Wi-Fi and BLE. Telemetry to a phone, a MAVLink bridge over Wi-Fi, sensors, indication, small scenarios. No Linux, but instant boot and milliwatts. - Raspberry Pi — Linux, Python, a camera. MAVLink routing, a video stream, mission scripts, logs. The standard first companion. - Jetson / Orange Pi with an NPU — when you need real-time neural networks. Protocols and roles ArduPilot expects MAVLink 2 on SERIALx_PROTOCOL = 2 ; PX4 on the companion port uses the same MAVLink or uXRCE-DDS for ROS 2. For Betaflight/INAV a companion in the classic sense is rare: they have MSP, and an onboard computer is usually needed only for video and telemetry. MAVLink routing One FC port, several consumers a GCS over 4G, a script on the companion, a logger : you need a router. mavlink-router C++, a systemd service, a config with UART/UDP/TCP endpoints or mavproxy.py --master=/dev/ttyAMA0 --out=udp:gcs-ip:14550 --out=udp:127.0.0.1:14551 — each client gets a copy of the stream, and commands go back to the FC. The companion port UART speed: 921600 baud SERIALx_BAUD = 921 — otherwise the port chokes with SRx_ streams at 10–50 Hz. The streams are configured from the companion REQUEST_DATA_STREAM / SET_MESSAGE_INTERVAL , not by default. {{diagram:mavlink-routing A typical onboard MAVLink routing scheme with a companion.}} Latency and what you can delegate to the companion The “companion → FC → response” command loop: UART 1–5 ms + FC processing + velocity loop dynamics of 0.3–1 s. That is fine for “fly to a point” and target tracking the “Tracking” module , but not for stabilization. The companion must not: control the motors, replace the EKF except supplying ExternalNav as a source , bypass the failsafe. The companion may: GUIDED/Offboard targets, missions, parameters, ExternalNav/optical flow as a source, the camera and video, logs to the cloud, the operator interface. Power, heat, failure Raspberry Pi 4/5 — 1–3 A at 5 V with peaks up to 5 A: a separate 5 V/5 A BEC, not an FC pad the “Connecting peripherals” module ; Jetson Orin Nano — 7–15 W, 19 V or 5 V/4 A depending on the module; a heatsink and airflow are mandatory — with thermal throttling, latency grows unpredictably. A companion failure hang, reboot, broken UART — the FC must survive it: GUIDED timeouts, a GCS failsafe with a deliberate action, a pilot with a no-companion mode on a switch. This is tested by pulling the UART in SITL/on the bench. Three typical architectures 1. Telemetry and bridge : an ESP32 with bridge firmware MAVLink over Wi-Fi/BLE to a phone, DroneBridge-class — decides nothing, only relays. 2. Pi + camera + scripts : Raspberry Pi 4/5, mavlink-router, Python mission scripts, a video stream to the GCS, optical flow/rangefinder over MAVLink. The standard for learning and prototypes. 3. Jetson + ROS 2 : detection/VIO on the GPU, PX4 via uXRCE-DDS or ArduPilot via MAVROS/AP_DDS, nodes with safeguards the “Tracking” module . For serious autonomy. Starter repositories for 2 and 3 are in examples/ in the course repository. practice Choosing a platform for the task 1. Telemetry on a screen, indication, setup from a phone — ESP32. 2. Video, MAVLink routing, Python scenarios — Raspberry Pi. 3. Object recognition, tracking — Jetson. Architecture checklist before a project 1. What does the aircraft do if the companion shuts down in flight? The answer must be “switches to mode X on a timeout”. 2. Which port and at what speed does MAVLink run on? Is there enough bandwidth for telemetry and commands? 3. How is the companion powered? Not from the FC telemetry port. 4. Who logs: the FC to the SD card, the companion its own logs. Do the timestamps match? 5. How do you update the companion software in the field? The observer code and what you should get python import time from pymavlink import mavutil own identity: system 1 this vehicle , component 191 = onboard computer m = mavutil.mavlink_connection "tcp:127.0.0
