title: From ROS 1 to ROS 2: reading old projects and porting them
summary: ROS 1 Noetic закончил поддержку в мае 2025 года, но половина открытых дроновых проектов, статей и туториалов — на ROS 1: MAVROS 1, catkin-воркспейсы, launch в XML, `rospy`. Модуль учит быстро читать такой проект («что здесь главное и что от чего зависит»), знать соответствия понятий ROS 1 → ROS 2, р
headings: Чем ROS 2 отличается по существу Как читать ROS 1 проект за 30 минут Перенос или мост Типовые замены в коде (Python) MAVROS 1 → MAVROS 2 Шаг 1. Чтение проекта Шаг 2. Эталонные данные Шаг 3. Перенос Шаг 4. Отчёт
text: summary ROS 1 Noetic закончил поддержку в мае 2025 года, но половина открытых дроновых проектов, статей и туториалов — на ROS 1: MAVROS 1, catkin-воркспейсы, launch в XML, rospy . Модуль учит быстро читать такой проект «что здесь главное и что от чего зависит» , знать соответствия понятий ROS 1 → ROS 2, решать, переносить или запускать рядом через мост, и переносить небольшой пакет. Лабораторная: перенос узла ROS 1 на ROS 2 с сохранением поведения, проверенный на записанных данных. theory Чем ROS 2 отличается по существу ROS 1 ROS 2 Что это меняет --- --- --- roscore master — центральный узел имён нет master, DDS discovery нет единой точки отказа; нужны домены/ограничение discovery TCPROS/UDPROS DDS с QoS надо думать о QoS модуль ros2-basics rospy , roscpp rclpy , rclcpp API другой, но идеи те же catkin, catkin_make / catkin build ament, colcon build другая сборка, package.xml format 3 launch XML .launch launch Python/XML/YAML .launch.py логика в launch-файле параметры в глобальном сервере параметры у каждого узла rosparam → ros2 param к конкретному узлу rosbag .bag ros2 bag SQLite3/MCAP конвертеры есть rosbags tf tf2 был и в ROS 1 почти без изменений nodelets компоненты composable nodes несколько узлов в одном процессе без копирования MAVROS 1 MAVROS 2 mavros в ROS 2 те же плагины, другие имена сервисов/QoS Как читать ROS 1 проект за 30 минут 1. Корень : package.xml / CMakeLists.txt — зависимости что за датчики, MAVROS ли, OpenCV ли . 2. Launch-файлы launch/ .launch — что запускается, с какими параметрами и remap-ами. Это «схема системы». 3. Узлы scripts/ .py , src/ .cpp : найдите init_node , Subscriber , Publisher , Service , Timer / Rate . Нарисуйте граф: что слушает, что публикует. 4. Параметры config/ .yaml , rospy.get_param — что настраивается. 5. Сообщения msg/ , srv/ — свои типы. 6. MAVROS-специфика : /mavros/setpoint_ , /mavros/set_mode , /mavros/cmd/arming — где проект управляет аппаратом и в какой системе координат. Итог — граф узлов как в ros2-basics и список внешних зависимостей. С ним понятно, сколько стоит перенос. Перенос или мост - ros1_bridge — двунаправленный мост топиков/сервисов между ROS 1 и ROS 2 при запущенных обоих. Требует совместимой сборки одинаковые типы сообщений с обеих сторон , исторически — Noetic + Foxy/Humble из исходников. После окончания поддержки Noetic это временное решение. - Перенос — правильный путь для живого кода. Порядок: сообщения → библиотечный код без ROS вынести! → узлы → launch → тесты на записанных данных. - Запуск ROS 1 в контейнере — для «посмотреть, как это работало» и для записи эталонных данных до переноса. Типовые замены в коде Python ROS 1 rospy ROS 2 rclpy --- --- rospy.init_node "n" rclpy.init ; node = Node "n" rospy.Subscriber "/t", T, cb node.create_subscription T, "/t", cb, qos rospy.Publisher "/t", T, queue_size=10 node.create_publisher T, "/t", 10 rospy.Rate 20 ; while not rospy.is_shutdown : ... rate.sleep node.create_timer 0.05, tick ; rclpy.spin node rospy.get_param "~alt", 5.0 node.declare_parameter "alt", 5.0 ; node.get_parameter "alt" .value rospy.ServiceProxy "/s", S req cli = node.create_client S, "/s" ; cli.call_async req rospy.Time.now node.get_clock .now rospy.loginfo ... node.get_logger .info ... Главная смена мышления — цикл while с rate.sleep заменяется таймером и колбэками , а синхронный вызов сервиса внутри колбэка — асинхронным, иначе узел заблокирует сам себя тот же executor обслуживает ответ . MAVROS 1 → MAVROS 2 Имена топиков в основном те же /mavros/state , /mavros/local_position/pose , /mavros/setpoint_position/local , но: QoS телеметрии — sensor data; некоторые сервисы и параметры переименованы; запуск — ros2 launch mavros apm.launch fcu_url:=... или px4.launch . Для PX4 в ROS 2 вместо MAVROS обычно переходят на uXRCE-DDS модуль ros2-px4 , для ArduPilot — на AP_DDS там, где его функций хватает модуль ros2-ardupilot . {{diagram:ros1-migration Что делать со старым проектом ROS 1: временный мост, перенос, MAVROS 2 или переписать по идеям.}} practice Шаг 1. Чтение проекта Возьмите открытый ROS 1 дроновый проект например, пример offboard из документации PX4 для ROS 1 / MAVROS или любой репозиторий с MAVROS 1 . За 30 минут нарисуйте граф узлов, список зависимостей и где проект управляет аппаратом. Шаг 2. Эталонные данные Если есть возможность — запустите проект в контейнере ROS 1 Noetic с SITL и запишите rosbag входов и выходов узла. Если нет — используйте bag из открытых источников или синтетические входы. Шаг 3. Перенос Перенесите один узел до ~200 строк : логику без ROS — в отдельный модуль с pytest-тестами как offboard_fsm.py , узел — тонкая обёртка rclpy . Сконвертируйте bag в формат ROS 2 пакет rosbags : rosbags-convert и проверьте, что выходы перенесённого узла совпадают с эталонными. Шаг 4. Отчёт Таблица: что заменено, сколько строк логики стало тестируемыми без ROS, какие различия в поведении найдены обычно — QoS и время . Лабораторная засчитывается, когда есть граф исходного проекта, перенесённый узел с тестами логики и сравнение выходов на одних и тех же данных. diagnostics - Симптом: перенесённый узел «зависает» на вызове сервиса - Возможная причина: синхронный вызов в колбэке однопоточного executor-а. - Что сделать: call_async + обработка future, или отдельная группа колбэков. - Симптом: узел не получает телеметрию MAVROS 2 - Возможная причина: QoS sensor data у издателя или другое имя топика. - Что сделать: ros2 topic info -v , профиль подписки. - Симптом: параметры «не применяются» - Возможная причина: в ROS 2 параметр нужно объявить declare_parameter и передать конкретному узлу. - Что сделать: объявление в конструкторе, YAML с именем узла в launch. - Симптом: ros1_bridge не передаёт свой тип сообщения - Возможная причина: мост собран без этого типа или определения различаются. - Что сделать: собрать мост из исходников с обоими воркспейсами; лучше — переносить. references - ROS 2 — Migration guide from ROS 1 https://docs.ros.org/en/jazzy/How-To-Guides/Migrating-from-ROS1.html primary A - ros1

title: PID
summary: Proportional-integral-derivative controller: P reacts to the current error, I accumulates the steady-state error, D damps fast changes.

title: Feedforward (FF)
summary: A contribution to the motor command taken directly from stick movement, before any error appears. Speeds up the start of a move.

title: Setpoint
summary: The desired angular rate (from sticks and rates) that the PID compares the gyro readings against.

title: Gyro
summary: A three-axis angular rate sensor. The main stabilization sensor, read thousands of times per second.

title: T/W (thrust-to-weight)
summary: The ratio of the maximum thrust of all motors to the takeoff weight. 2:1 is the minimum for controlled flight.

title: Mixer
summary: A table that converts throttle, roll, pitch and yaw into a command for each motor depending on the frame type.

title: KV
summary: Motor RPM per volt with no load. Low KV for big props, high KV for small ones.

title: ESC
summary: Electronic speed controller: commutates the phases of a brushless motor based on commands from the FC.

title: DShot
summary: A digital FC → ESC protocol: a 16-bit packet with a checksum, no calibration. The number is the speed in kbit/s.

title: Bidirectional DShot
summary: DShot with a return channel: the ESC reports motor eRPM. The basis of the RPM filter.

title: RPM filter
summary: A bank of narrow notch filters at each motor's rotation frequency and its harmonics, driven by bidirectional DShot data.

title: Dynamic notch
summary: An automatic notch filter that finds peaks in the gyro spectrum and suppresses them.

title: D-term
summary: The derivative term of the PID. Sensitive to noise: with poor filtering it heats up the motors.

title: Blackbox
summary: Betaflight log: gyro, setpoint, PID, motors, RC at a high rate, for post-flight analysis.

title: Bounce-back
summary: Gyro rebound in the opposite direction after the stick stops; a metric of underdamping.

title: Entry lag
summary: Time from the start of a setpoint move until the gyro reaches 50% of it. The "sluggish on the sticks" metric.

title: Propwash
summary: Shaking when the vehicle flies into its own turbulent downwash, usually during descent.

title: diff all
summary: A Betaflight CLI command that outputs only the differences of the configuration from the defaults. The unit for storing a config.

title: Resource remap
summary: Reassigning a function (motor, UART, LED) to another board pad via the CLI.

title: craft_name
summary: The craft name in the Betaflight config. A reliable drone identifier for scripts instead of a COM port number.

title: UART
summary: Serial port: receiver, GPS, VTX, telemetry. Wires crossed over, common GND.

title: Inverted signal
summary: UART with inverted logic levels: idle is low. The SBUS standard; F4 can't invert in hardware.

title: SBUS
summary: A receiver → FC protocol from Futaba/FrSky: 100 kbaud, 8E2, inverted, one-way.

title: CRSF
summary: The TBS Crossfire and ExpressLRS protocol: a regular UART, full duplex, channels and telemetry over a single port.

title: ELRS (ExpressLRS)
summary: An open-source radio control system: choice of packet rate, telemetry ratio, 2.4 GHz and 900 MHz.

title: Packet rate
summary: The number of control packets per second. Higher means lower latency and worse sensitivity.

title: LQ (link quality)
summary: Fraction of successful packets out of the last 100. RSSI is the power margin; you need both together.

title: VTX
summary: Video transmitter. Controlled by the FC over SmartAudio/Tramp/MSP according to the VTX table.

title: vtxtable
summary: The table of VTX bands, channels and power levels in Betaflight. FACTORY sends the channel number, CUSTOM sends the frequency.

title: OSD
summary: Telemetry overlaid on the video in the goggles: voltage, time, link, warnings.

title: Arming disable flags
summary: Betaflight flags that prevent arming (RXLOSS, THROTTLE, ANGLE, MSP…). Visible via status and in the OSD.

title: Failsafe
summary: Behavior on link loss. In Betaflight: Stage 1 (guard time) and Stage 2 (DROP, AUTO-LAND, GPS_RESCUE).

title: BEC
summary: An onboard voltage regulator (5/9/12 V) for the FC, receiver, camera and VTX.

title: C rating
summary: A battery's rated discharge current as a multiple of its capacity. Usually inflated; trust the log and the internal resistance.

title: Voltage sag
summary: The voltage drop under current across the battery's internal resistance: I × R.

title: Cloud Build
summary: Building Betaflight firmware on the server for a selected set of options (defines).

title: Target
summary: A firmware variant for a specific board: MCU, gyro, pins.

title: ArduPilot
summary: An open-source autopilot: Copter, Plane, Rover, Sub. Navigation, missions, Lua, companion.

title: FRAME_CLASS / FRAME_TYPE
summary: ArduPilot parameters: frame type (Quad=1, Hexa=2, Octa=3, OctaQuad=4, Tri=7) and layout (X=1, Plus=0…).

title: Pre-arm checks
summary: ArduPilot checks before arming: calibrations, EKF, link, parameters. A PreArm message is a hint, not an obstacle.

title: GCS
summary: Ground control station: Mission Planner, QGroundControl, MAVProxy. Talks to the FC over MAVLink.

title: SITL
summary: Software In The Loop: the real firmware running on a PC with a physics simulator in place of sensors.

title: MAVProxy
summary: ArduPilot's command-line ground station in Python. Launched together with SITL.

title: pymavlink
summary: Python MAVLink library: connection, reading messages, commands. Low level, everything visible.

title: MAVSDK
summary: A high-level SDK on top of MAVLink (C++, Python): arm(), takeoff(), telemetry subscriptions.

title: MAVLink
summary: The FC ↔ GCS/companion protocol: packets with a message ID, system_id, component_id and a CRC based on the XML definition.

title: Heartbeat
summary: A MAVLink message sent once per second by every participant: type, mode, armed state. No heartbeat, no link.

title: COMMAND_ACK
summary: MAVLink command acknowledgment with a result. A command without an ACK check is hope, not control.

title: GUIDED
summary: An ArduPilot mode in which position/velocity targets are set by an external source (GCS, companion).

title: NED
summary: North-East-Down coordinate frame: Z points down, climbing is negative Z.

title: EKF
summary: Extended Kalman filter: fuses IMU, GPS, baro and compass into a single estimate of position, velocity and attitude.

title: Lane switching
summary: EKF switching between cores (per IMU) to a healthier one.

title: DCM
summary: A simple complementary attitude filter in ArduPilot. A backup to the EKF; works without GPS and compass.

title: DataFlash
summary: ArduPilot's onboard binary log (.bin): VIBE, ATT, CTUN, BAT, ERR, XKF and hundreds of other messages.

title: VIBE
summary: An ArduPilot log message with per-axis vibration and an accelerometer clipping counter. Below 30 is normal.

title: Mission
summary: A list of commands for AUTO mode: NAV (where to go), DO (what to do), CONDITION (when).

title: Home
summary: Copter's arming point. RTL returns here, not to the pilot.

title: Lua scripts (ArduPilot)
summary: Onboard scripts: switches, sensors, scenarios. Require ≥2 MB of flash, do not run on F4.

title: Fault injection
summary: Deliberate injection of failures (motor, sensor) in SITL to test the behavior of the vehicle and the pilot.

title: OctaQuad (X8)
summary: Four arms with two coaxial motors each. Fault tolerance at the cost of ~15% thrust loss.

title: QuadPlane
summary: VTOL in ArduPlane: takes off like a multirotor, flies like a plane.

title: Tilt-rotor
summary: VTOL with tilting motors. Q_TILT_* parameters, TiltMotor* output functions.

title: SERVOn_FUNCTION
summary: The function of an FC output in ArduPilot: motor, tilt servo, control surface. A mismatch with the wiring is dangerous.

title: Companion computer
summary: An onboard computer for vision, scenarios, networking. It advises via GUIDED; the FC decides.

title: mavlink-router
summary: A MAVLink router: one UART, many consumers over UDP/TCP.

title: systemd service
summary: A way to start a script on a Linux companion automatically and restart it after a crash.

title: EdgeTX
summary: Open-source radio firmware (TX16S and others) with Lua scripts and an AUX port in Lua mode.

title: ESP32
summary: A microcontroller with Wi-Fi and BLE: peripherals, MAVLink bridge, radio companion.

title: Kt (torque constant)
summary: Motor torque per amp of current, Kt = 60/(2π·KV) N·m/A; low KV = high torque per amp.

title: FSPL
summary: Free-space signal loss: 20·log(d) + 20·log(f) + 32.44 dB; +6 dB per doubling of range.

title: Link budget
summary: The sum of power, antenna gains and losses minus FSPL versus receiver sensitivity; margin ≥ 10–15 dB.

title: SWR
summary: Standing wave ratio: the fraction of power reflected by the antenna back into the transmitter; 1.0 is ideal, ≤ 2 is acceptable.

title: Circular polarization
summary: The field rotates (RHCP/LHCP); less sensitive to orientation and reflections; never mix RHCP and LHCP.

title: Low-ESR capacitor
summary: An electrolytic/polymer capacitor on the power bus that absorbs voltage spikes caused by wire inductance during ESC switching.

title: Smoke stopper
summary: A current limiter (bulb/resistor) in series with the positive lead at first power-up: a short circuit won't burn the board.

title: Hard iron / soft iron
summary: Compass errors: a constant offset from magnetized parts (hard iron) and field distortion from ferromagnetic materials (soft iron); calibrated with offsets and a matrix.

title: Bias
summary: The sensor output at zero input; for a gyro it integrates into attitude drift; estimated by the EKF.

title: Quaternion
summary: Four numbers with unit norm describing attitude without gimbal lock; the firmware standard.

title: Complementary filter
summary: Fusing the gyro (high frequencies) with the accelerometer/compass (low frequencies) using fixed coefficients; a special case of the Kalman filter.

title: Innovation
summary: The difference between a measurement and the filter's prediction; if the normalized innovation exceeds the gate, the measurement is rejected.

title: Kalman gain
summary: The weight given to a measurement versus the prediction, computed from the covariances; the adaptive counterpart of the complementary filter's K.

title: HDOP
summary: A multiplier on GNSS horizontal error due to satellite geometry; < 1 is excellent, > 2.5 is poor.

title: RTK
summary: Real-Time Kinematic: carrier-phase corrections from a base station give centimeter accuracy; requires a pair of dual-frequency receivers.

title: Optical flow
summary: The angular rate of the image moving under the camera; combined with rangefinder altitude and the gyro, it gives linear velocity.

title: EK3_SRC
summary: EKF3 source sets (position, velocity, altitude, heading): GPS, baro, rangefinder, optical flow, external navigation; switchable in flight.

title: Phase margin
summary: Degrees short of −180° at the loop's unity-gain frequency; delay eats into it linearly with frequency.

title: Damping ζ
summary: A parameter of a second-order loop: ζ ≈ 0.7 gives ~5% overshoot; low ζ means bounce-back and ringing.

title: Aliasing
summary: Frequencies above fs/2 showing up at false frequencies after sampling; fixed with an anti-aliasing filter and full-rate logging.

title: Group delay
summary: The delay a filter adds to the useful signal; PT1 ≈ 1/(2π·fc).

title: Welch's method
summary: Spectrum estimation by averaging FFTs over overlapping windows; resolution fs/nperseg.

title: Overshoot
summary: Response overshoot past the setpoint after a step, in percent; related to damping.

title: TECS
summary: Total energy control for a wing: throttle sets the total energy, the elevator sets the split between altitude and airspeed.

title: Stall speed
summary: V_s = √(2mg/(ρ·S·C_Lmax)); in a turn it grows as 1/√cos φ.

title: Stability margin
summary: The distance of the CG ahead of the neutral point as a fraction of MAC; 5–15% is normal.

title: Harmonic notch (ArduPilot)
summary: Harmonic notch filter `INS_HNTCH_*` with tracking by throttle, ESC telemetry or FFT.

title: AUTOTUNE
summary: Automatic tuning of rate/angle gains from a series of "twitches" on an axis in hover.

title: FMEA
summary: Failure Modes and Effects Analysis: failure → effect → detection → RPN → mitigation → verification.

title: Dead reckoning
summary: Dead reckoning from inertial sensors and wind without external measurements; accurate for seconds to tens of seconds.

title: DroneCAN
summary: A protocol over CAN for autopilot peripherals: nodes with IDs, standard messages, 120 Ω terminators.

title: CAN arbitration
summary: Resolving simultaneous transmission: a dominant 0 wins, the lower ID wins without losing time.

title: DMA
summary: Direct memory access: peripherals exchange data with memory without the CPU (DShot, SPI gyro, UART).

title: Jitter
summary: Variation in a task's actual period; grows with locking and long interrupts.

title: Work queue (PX4)
summary: Prioritized work queues in which most PX4 modules run on NuttX.

title: Traceability matrix
summary: A requirement ↔ test ↔ result table; empty cells are open requirements.

title: ADR
summary: Architecture Decision Record: context, options, decision, consequences.

title: VIO
summary: Visual-inertial odometry: position and attitude from features in frames and the IMU; drift of 0.5–2% of distance traveled.

title: ExternalNav
summary: External navigation source for EKF3 (VISION_POSITION_ESTIMATE/ODOMETRY), `EK3_SRC* = 6`.

title: Precision / Recall
summary: Fraction of correct detections among those found / fraction found among the true ones; the confidence threshold trades one for the other.

title: Glass-to-glass latency
summary: Time from an event in front of the camera to its appearance on the screen; measured with a timer in the frame.

title: Offboard (PX4)
summary: Control mode from a companion with a setpoint stream ≥ 2 Hz; timeout COM_OF_LOSS_T.

title: Spot welding
summary: Spot welding nickel strip to 18650/21700 cells; soldering to cells is not allowed.

title: BMS
summary: Battery management system: voltage/current/temperature protection and balancing; cutting off discharge in flight is dangerous.

title: Thrust stand
summary: Measuring a motor's thrust/current/power with a prop; checking the build sheet's calculations against reality.

title: Engineering folder
summary: Requirements with IDs, tests and a project changelog are a mandatory part of every capstone project.

title: Troubleshooting tree
summary: A "symptom → branch → measurement → cause" sequence of checks for finding a fault.

title: Near miss
summary: A near miss with no damage; the main source of improvements to the field protocol.

title: L1 navigation
summary: ArduPlane's guidance algorithm: the vehicle aims at a point on the route line a distance L1 ahead and commands lateral acceleration based on the angle to it. The NAVL1_PERIOD sets how aggressive it is.

title: Pure pursuit
summary: "Pursuit" guidance: a point at lookahead distance L is chosen on the path, and the vehicle turns toward it with curvature 2·sin(η)/L. A larger L is smoother but cuts corners.

title: S-curve (jerk-limited)
summary: A jerk-limited velocity profile: acceleration ramps up smoothly instead of stepping. This is how ArduPilot (WP_JERK) and PX4 build trajectories.

title: Chirp
summary: A test signal whose frequency rises smoothly from f₀ to f₁. The response to it is used to build the loop's frequency response.

title: Coherence
summary: A measure from 0 to 1 of how much of the output is linearly explained by the input at a given frequency. Below ~0.6, a point on the frequency response is not worth using.

title: AP_Periph
summary: ArduPilot firmware for DroneCAN peripheral nodes: GPS, compass, airspeed sensor, ESC adapter on a separate STM32.

title: Node ID
summary: A node's number on the DroneCAN bus (1–127). Set statically or assigned by the dynamic node allocation (DNA) server on the autopilot.

title: Conducted interference
summary: Noise conducted along power and ground wires (ripple from ESCs and converters), not through the air. Fixed with an LC filter and a low-ESR capacitor at the source.

title: DRC
summary: Design Rule Check: automatic check of a board for clearances, trace widths and vias against the fab's rules. Zero DRC errors is the condition for sending it to production.

title: Gerber
summary: The set of board layer files (copper, solder mask, silkscreen, outline) plus a drill file: what the fab receives.

title: Clamp meter
summary: An instrument that measures current from the magnetic field around a wire without breaking the circuit. DC requires a Hall-effect clamp.

title: Fault tolerance
summary: The vehicle's ability to survive the failure of a single component (motor, BEC, receiver) and land under control. A quadcopter does not have it for motors; a hexa and an X8 can, given spare thrust, well-designed power and a firmware response verified in SITL or on a bench.

title: Cold solder joint
summary: A cold solder joint: dull, lumpy, with poor wetting. Holds on the bench and fails under vibration.

title: Strain relief
summary: Securing a wire near a solder joint or connector so bending and vibration don't break the strands at the joint.

title: Config diff
summary: A line-by-line comparison of two parameter dumps. A config in git plus a diff before flight shows what changed since last time.

title: Weight budget
summary: A table of the weights of all components versus the target takeoff weight. Determines the thrust-to-weight ratio and flight time before you buy anything.

title: Ohm's law
summary: U = I·R: the voltage across an element equals the current times the resistance. Power P = U·I.

title: Bluejay
summary: Open-source firmware for ESCs on 8-bit EFM8 BB21 and BB51 (BB1 only up to version 0.18.1), the successor to BLHeli_S, with bidirectional DShot for the RPM filter.

title: AM32
summary: Open-source firmware for 32-bit ARM ESCs (STM32, AT32, GD32, etc.), a replacement for BLHeli_32.

title: Frame resonance
summary: The frequency at which a frame or arm oscillates on its own. If it matches the motor speed frequency, vibration grows and the gyros get noisy.

title: Moment of inertia
summary: A measure of resistance to rotation: J = Σ m·r². Mass far from the center makes the vehicle sluggish in roll and pitch.

title: Remote ID
summary: Broadcasting the ID, coordinates and altitude of the vehicle and the pilot during flight (Bluetooth / Wi-Fi). A regulatory requirement in many countries.

title: MAVLink signing
summary: A MAVLink 2 mechanism: every packet is signed with a shared secret key and a timestamp. Rejects foreign commands and replays of intercepted ones.

title: Scheduler
summary: The part of the firmware that runs tasks at a given rate and priority: gyro loop, PID, RX, OSD. The first thing you look for when reading the source.

title: Position hold
summary: GPS position hold mode: the vehicle counters wind drift by itself. In INAV it is NAV POSHOLD.

title: INAV
summary: A Cleanflight fork with navigation: position hold, RTH, missions, wings and rovers.

title: Logic condition (INAV)
summary: A line of the INAV Programming Framework: a condition on flags and values whose result triggers an action or feeds other conditions.

title: Waypoint
summary: A mission waypoint: coordinates, altitude and an action (fly-through, loiter, RTH, landing).

title: Elevons
summary: The two control surfaces of a flying wing that combine elevator and ailerons: deflected together for pitch, in opposite directions for roll.

title: OpenIPC
summary: Open-source firmware for IP cameras that turns them into a digital FPV transmitter over Wi-Fi adapters in packet injection mode.

title: SiK
summary: Open-source firmware for 433/868/915 MHz telemetry modems with frequency hopping; used by 3DR Radio and RFD900.

title: Rotation matrix
summary: An orthogonal 3×3 matrix with determinant 1 that transforms a vector from one coordinate frame to another. Its inverse equals its transpose.

title: Gimbal lock
summary: Loss of one degree of freedom in Euler angles at ±90° pitch: roll and yaw become the same axis. That is why quaternions are used internally.

title: Natural frequency ωn
summary: The frequency at which an undamped second-order system oscillates. Together with ζ it sets the settling time and overshoot.

title: Euler method
summary: The simplest numerical integration: x(t+dt) = x(t) + f(x)·dt. Unstable with a large step, hence the loop-rate requirements.

title: Covariance
summary: A measure of how two quantities vary together. The EKF covariance matrix describes how confident the filter is in each component of the state.

title: Component ID
summary: A component's number within a vehicle in MAVLink (autopilot 1, camera 100, gimbal 154, etc.). Together with the system ID it forms the address.

title: System ID
summary: The vehicle's number on a MAVLink network (1–255). Two vehicles on the same network must have different ones: in ArduPilot 4.7 the parameter is MAV_SYSID.

title: CRC_EXTRA
summary: A byte computed from the message definition and mixed into the MAVLink CRC. Catches dialect version mismatches between sender and receiver.

title: MAVLink dialect
summary: XML description of a message set (common, ardupilotmega, development). Both sides must be built from the same dialect.

title: UDP broadcast / unicast
summary: Ways of delivering MAVLink over a network: broadcast goes to everyone on the subnet, unicast goes to a single address. Over 4G/NAT and L3 VPNs (WireGuard, Tailscale, OpenVPN tun) only unicast works; broadcast only passes through L2 tunnels (ZeroTier, OpenVPN tap).

title: MAVROS
summary: A ROS package that bridges MAVLink to ROS topics and services. Superseded by uXRCE-DDS for PX4; for ArduPilot it remains alongside AP_DDS.

title: MAVLink microservice
summary: A protocol on top of messages for one task: parameters, missions, commands, FTP. Defines the exchange order and retries on packet loss.

title: Root cause
summary: The cause lies in the process, not in a person or a part: why the failure was possible at all. You eliminate it, or the crash repeats with a different part.

title: Vehicle log
summary: A record of flight time, battery cycles, replacements and incidents for each vehicle. The basis for life-based scheduled maintenance.

title: Density altitude
summary: The altitude in the standard atmosphere with the same air density as right now. Heat and high elevation raise it, and props produce less thrust.

title: Gimbal Manager
summary: A role in the MAVLink Gimbal v2 protocol: the component that parses requests from the GCS and companion and commands the gimbal (Gimbal Device).

title: OBSTACLE_DISTANCE
summary: A MAVLink message with 72 sectors of distances to obstacles around the vehicle. ArduPilot and PX4 use it to brake and avoid.

title: INT8 quantization
summary: Converting network weights and activations from float to 8-bit integers. Speeds up inference 2–4× on NPU/TensorRT at the cost of a small accuracy loss; verified on a validation set.

title: Camera matrix K
summary: Camera intrinsics: focal lengths f_x, f_y in pixels and the principal point c_x, c_y. Maps a ray to a pixel and back; found by checkerboard calibration.

title: LANDING_TARGET
summary: A MAVLink message the companion uses to send the autopilot the angular offset or position of a marker for precision landing.

title: GSD
summary: Ground Sample Distance: how many centimeters of ground one image pixel covers. GSD = altitude · pixel size / focal length.

title: Image overlap
summary: The fraction of shared area between adjacent frames along and across the route. For photogrammetry it is usually 70–80 % along and 60–70 % across.

title: Image-plane error
summary: The target's offset from the image center (or a set point) in pixels or normalized coordinates. The outer tracking loop turns it into a velocity command.

title: Jetson Orin
summary: A family of NVIDIA modules with an Ampere GPU (Orin NX/AGX also have DLA accelerators) for onboard inference. A typical companion for PX4 and ArduPilot.

title: uORB
summary: PX4's internal publish-subscribe message bus between modules. uXRCE-DDS exposes selected uORB topics to ROS 2.

title: Cascaded controller
summary: Nested loops: position commands velocity, velocity commands angle, angle commands angular rate. The inner loop is tuned first and made several times faster than the outer one.

title: Lifecycle node
summary: A ROS 2 node with explicit unconfigured → inactive → active states and transitions between them. Gives controlled startup and shutdown of an onboard application.

title: AP_DDS
summary: The eProsima Micro XRCE-DDS client built into ArduPilot: publishes state to ROS 2 and accepts commands without MAVLink; on the ROS 2 side it is served by an agent (`micro_ros_agent` or Micro XRCE-DDS Agent).

title: QoS
summary: Quality of Service in ROS 2: reliability, queue depth, durability. A publisher and a subscriber with incompatible QoS don't connect, and there is no error: the subscriber simply receives nothing (the log only shows an "incompatible QoS" warning).

title: tf2
summary: The ROS library for the tree of coordinate frames over time: map → odom → base_link → camera. Answers where the sensor was at the moment a frame was captured.

title: ros1_bridge
summary: A bridge that forwards topics between ROS 1 and ROS 2 during a migration. Requires both distributions to be installed side by side.

title: Costmap
summary: A costmap in Nav2: cells weighted by traversability, built from obstacles with an inflation margin. Paths are planned on it.

title: uXRCE-DDS

title: Project 1: Web GCS: telemetry, map, flight modes
summary: A ground control station in the browser: the backend reads MAVLink and serves telemetry over WebSocket; the frontend draws the vehicle on a map, shows the flight mode, battery and STATUSTEXT, and can arm and change modes with confirmation.

title: Project 2: Fleet telemetry to the cloud + dashboard
